1:2.text: People are of two types: The one who affirms [the existence] of the Truth [Allāh] and the one who denies Him. So the opening chapter (al-Fātiḥah) comprises an affirmation of the Exalted Creator and a refutation of the one who denies Him by affirming His Lordship—the Exalted—over the worlds
1:2.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

2:3.text: Regarding the statement ...and spend out of what We have provided for them...: Allāh the Exalted often combines between [the mention of] prayer (ṣalāḥ) and charity (zakāh) in the Qurʾān because prayer comprises sincerity (ikhlāṣ) to the Deity [Allāh] and charity and spending comprise benevolence (iḥsān) to His servants. Thus, the sign of the servant’s happiness is sincerity to the Deity and striving to benefit the creation. Just as the sign of the servant’s misery is the absence of these two affairs, there being neither sincerity [to the Deity] and nor benevolence [to the creation].
2:3.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

2:19.text: This similitude has been struck by Allāh for the Qurʾān and the behaviour of the disbelievers and hypocrites towards it. The rain is the Qurʾān because it gives life to the hearts, just as the rain gives life to the bodies. The darknesses represent what is in the Qurʾān of the mention of disbelief (kufr) and associationism (shirk). The thunder represents the threats [in the Qurʾān] by which they are frightened, and likewise, the mention of the Fire. And the lightning is what the Qurʾān contains of guidance, clarification, promises [of forgiveness and reward] and the mention of Paradise. The disbelievers block their hearing when the Qurʾān is being recited, out of fear that their hearts might incline towards it. This is because faith (īmān) to them is disbelief (kufr) and kufr is death.
2:19.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

2:21.text: Meaning, single out (waḥḥadū) your Lord in worship. Ibn ʿAbbās—may Allāh be pleased with him—said: “Everything related in the Qurʾān with respect to worship (ʿibādah), then its meaning is tawḥīd [to single out Allāh with worship].
2:21.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

2:62.text: The nations prior to the sending of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) are of two types. A type who are disbelievers, all of them wretched (in the hereafter) there being no happy person among them (who is successful in the hereafter), such as the idol-worshippers and the Magians. And a type who are divided into happy and wretched, and they are the Jews, Christians and Sabeans.
2:62.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

2:62.text: The Sabeans are a people who are not upon the religion of the Jews, nor the Christians, nor the Magians, nor the Polytheists. But they are a people who remain upon their original disposition (fiṭrah). They have no established religion that they follow and pursue. For this reason, the Polytheists would label the one who became a Muslims as a Sabean, with the meaning that he departed from all the religions of the people of the world. And some said that he Sabeans are those to whom the call of the Prophet never reached, and Allāh knows best.
2:62.author: Imām Ibn Katḥir (d. 774H)

2:74.text: Then your hearts became hardened, meaning, they became dry and cold, and this is when mercy and gentleness depart from the heart, ...after that , after the appearance of the evidences. And He did not resemble them with iron even though it is harder than stone. This is because iron can be made soft with the fire, and Dāwūd (عليه السلام) softened it in this manner, but stones are never softened. Then, stones were given virtue over the hardened heart And indeed, there are among the stones out of which rivers gushes forth. It is said that all stones are meant, and it is also said that it is the rock that Mūsā struck for the tribes. And indeed, there are among them from whose splitting water flows out. He intended springs which are less than rivers. And indeed among them—[the stones and the hearts] are those which fall down, when they fall from the top of the mountain to its bottom, out of awe of Allāh, whilst your hearts—O gathering of the Jews—do not soften and do not have awe.
2:74.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

2:121.text: Imām al-Ṭabarī brings the following reports: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿIkrimah: “They follow it as it truly should be followed.” Ibn ʿAbbās: “They accept as lawful what it makes lawful, accept as unlawful what it makes unlawful, and do not distort its words from their proper places.” Mujāhid: “They act upon it as it truly should be acted upon.” Ibn Masʿūd and Qatādah: “They treat as lawful what it makes lawful and treat as unlawful what it makes unlawful. They recite it as it was revealed by Allāh. They do not distort its words from their proper places and they do not explain anything of it with other than its (true) explanation.” Al-Ḥasan: “They act upon its decisive verses (muḥkam), believe in its ambiguous verses (mutashābih), and entrust the knowledge of what is difficult for them to its knower.”
2:121.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

2:121.text: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: “They are the Jews who believed (such as) ʿAbd Allāh bin Salām, Shuʿbah bin ʿAmr, Tamām bin Yahūdā, Asad and Usayd bin Kaʿb, Ibn Yāmīn and ʿAbd Allāh bin Ṣūriyā.
2:121.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

2:146.text: The Jews knew that a prophet was to appear in the deserts of Arabia, in the Ḥijāz region known as Paran (Fārān), and that Bakkah (Makkah) was a place that was inhabited by Ishmael and his offspring, wherein was the House built for Allāh’s worship, to which the Israelite prophets would make pilgrimage. And they knew that Allāh’s greater blessing would change from Bayt al-Maqdis to the land of Paran. Hence, when the qiblah (direction of prayer) was changed from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Kaʿbah, they pretended as if they did not know. But this was a tribulation, to test who would follow the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) from those who would turn on their heels, after knowing the truth.

2:157.text: These are the bounties from Allāh the Mighty and Majestic upon the patient ones who say, ‘To Allāh we belong and to Him shall we return’ after a calamity. And the ṣalāt of Allāh upon His servant is His forgiveness, mercy, blessing and honouring of him in this life and the hereafter. And al-Zajāj said: ‘The ṣalāt from Allāh the Mighty and Majestic is forgiveness and beautiful praise’.
2:157.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

2:157.text: Meaning, the praise from Allāh upon them.
2:157.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

2:157.text: Ṣalawāt, meaning mercy because ṣalāt from Allāh is mercy, and as for the mercy (raḥmah) which Allāh mentioned [after ṣalawāt], then it is for emphasis. And He made ṣalawāt plural, which means mercy after mercy.
2:157.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

2:157.text: The bounties from Allāh the Exalted upon the patient ones who say, ‘To Allāh we belong and to Him shall we return’ after a calamity. And the ṣalāt of Allāh upon His servant is His pardoning, mercy, blessing and honouring of him in this life and the hereafter. He repeated mercy [with its own word]—and it is from the greatest parts of ṣalāt—because it is a different word, as an emphasis from Him, the Exalted.
2:157.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah (d. 546H)

2:157.text: ( عَلَيْهِمْ صَلَوَاتٌ ) Ibn ʿAbbās said: “Forgiveness”. Ibn Kaysān said: Ṣalawāt here is praise, mercy and attestation for their integrity (tazkiyah). He mentioned ṣalāt and mercy—whilst their meaning is one—due to the variation in the two words. He also put ṣalawāt in plural because by way of it He meant mercy that comes after mercy. Editorial Note: From the meanings of ṣalāt is mercy, though it is not all of the meaning of ṣalāt, since ṣalāt has other meanings too. So whilst the meaning of ṣalāt and raḥmāh is one as it relates to the element of mercy, there are differences in the two words because ṣalāt comprises more than just the meaning of mercy. Hence, to emphasise mercy, it was repeated again separately with the word raḥmah.
2:157.author: Al-Thaʿlabī (d. 427H)

2:157.text: Editorial Note: The word “ṣalāt” is a composite term consisting of numerous meanings. Depending on whom it is ascribed to, it takes on some or all of those meanings. It has a technical meaning that refers to all the elements, conceptual and physical, found in the ritual prayer. Hence, standing, bowing, prostrating, invoking, love, hope, praise and so on are all part of the ritual prayer, just as it comprises blessing, bounty, mercy and forgiveness. When ascribed to the servant it takes on the whole or part of that meaning. Hence, ṣalāt from the servant is invocation (duʿā) or ritual prayer and its performance is praise, blessing, mercy and forgiveness for him. When ascribed to Allāh it refers to the conferring of some of the elements that it comprises such as praise, blessing, mercy, forgiveness and so on. Hence, when the servant makes ṣalāt, he is standing, bowing, prostrating, invoking, praising, seeking blessing, bounty, mercy, forgiveness, and ṣalāt incorporates all of these meanings. And the ṣalāt of Allāh is His conferring upon His servants, those elements such as praise, blessing and mercy which are comprised in prayer. The reason why Christian evangelists are using doubts in this subject matter is that they are unable to validate the foundations of their own religion: That their god was given birth to, after being in a womb for nine months, nourished by blood and exited through the private parts of a woman. That their god possessed a penis and an anus, that their god drank and ate and passed urine and stools. That their god was humiliated, killed and buried and so on. All people of sound mind will reject such falsehood, and likewise the falsehood of their other doctrines such as the trinity, original sin and so on, none of which were known to the Children of Israel but which were fabricated and innovated to make it easier for converts from Pagan backgrounds to accept Jesus. Hence, realising this and realising that they cannot argue for their innovated religion that was unknown to the Children of Israel at that time, they have decided to embark upon misdirection—away from these affairs which are the foundations of their religion and their idea of divinity—and instead to try to confuse Muslims using these types of technical discussions about the Qurʾān and its language, in which a certain degree of knowledge and understanding is required to counter their falsehood and which many Muslims may lack.

2:190.text: It is said that this verse is decisive (muḥkamah) and unabrogated. The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) was ordered to fight those who fought against him, and the meaning of His saying ...and do not transgress the limits..., do not kill women and children, the old man and the monk and those who make offer of peace.
2:190.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

2:190.text: And Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUmar bin ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz and Mujāhid said: ‘It is a decisive verse (muḥkamah).’ Meaning, fight those who are engaged in fighting against you, but do not transgress [the limits] by killing women, children, priests, monks and their likes. Abū Jaʿfar al-Nuḥās said: ‘This is the most correct of the two views [and is known by evidence of] the Sunnah and inspection. As for the Sunnah, it is the ḥadīth of Ibn ʿUmar that the Messenger of Allāh (صلى الله عليه وسلم) saw a woman who had been killed in one of his expeditions, and he disliked that and prohibited the killing of women and children. As for inspection, then the verb form (فاعل) is not used except for an action in which two parties participate, such as muqātalah (fighting), mushātamah (reviling), mukhāṣamah (arguing). And fighting is not participated in by women, children and those like them such as the priests, the terminally ill, the old and the hired labourers. They are not to be killed.
2:190.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d.671H)

2:253.text: His statement (مِّنْهُم مَّن كَلَّمَ ٱللَّهُ) Among them were those to whom Allāh spoke is a proof against the one who holds that the Qurʾān [which is Allāh's speech] is created and who negates the [attribute of] speech from Allāh. Allāh has informed about Himself—the Lofty and Exalted—that among the Messengers are those whom He spoke to [directly].
2:253.author: Al-Imām Muḥammad bin ʿAlī al-Qaṣṣāb (d. 360H)

3:64.text: The commentators (mufassirūn) said: The delegation of Najrān (who were Christians) came to Madīnah and met with the Jews, and they argued about Abraham (عليه السلام). The Christians claimed he was a Christian and that they are upon his religion and that they are the most worthy of people of (attachment to) him. And the Jews said that he was a Jew and that they are upon his religion and that they are the most worthy of people of (attachment to) him. So the Messenger of Allāh (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: ‘Both of you are free of Abraham and his religion, rather Abraham was a Ḥanīf (upright, person of Tawḥīd), Muslim, and I am upon his religion. So follow his religion, the religion of Islām.’ So the Jews said: ‘O Muḥammad, you do not wish except that we take you as a lord, just as the Christians took Jesus as a lord.’ And the Christians said: ‘O Muḥammad, you do not wish except that we say about you what the Jews said about Ezra.’ So then Allāh revealed [this verse].
3:64.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

3:64.text: Come to a just word, meaning a word of justice between us and you and the just word is that we single out Allāh [in Tawḥīd], so that we do not worship others besides Him and we free ourselves from every deity besides Him, so we do not associate anything with Him... As for his saying: ...that we worship none but Allāh (alone), it is in [the grammatical state of] khafḍ, with the meaning: “Come, [all of us], to not worshipping except Allāh (alone).”
3:64.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

3:186.text: He is Kaʿb bin al-Ashraf, it was revealed in relation to him. He used to be a poet and would abuse the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and his companions. He would also incite the disbelievers of Quraysh against him and would harass the Muslim women through flirtatious poetry. Prior to al-Qurṭubī, Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H) similarly explained that this verse was revealed in connection to Kaʿb bin al-Ashraf—a Jewish leader—who used to verbally abuse the Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم), incite the polytheists against the Muslims and harass Muslim women through flirtatious poetry.
3:186.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

3:186.text: That which is apparent is that [this verse] is not abrogated [by the verses of fighting]. For argumentation in ways that are best and amicable behaviour [when inviting them] is something commended. And [the Prophet] (صلى الله عليه وسلم) —alongside the command to fight [having already been revealed]—would maintain ties with the Jews and treat them courteously. He would also pardon the hypocrites [turning away from them], and this is clear [in establishing the point]. Refer to (16:125:) and (29:146:).
3:186.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

3:186.text: The Exalted informs and addresses the Believers that they will be put to trial in their material possessions by way of the obligatory and recommended spending [enjoined upon them] and by way of the expiration of their wealth through what they spend in the cause (path) of Allāh. Likewise, in their bodies through those burdens that are heavy upon many people, such as striving in the path of Allāh and being subject to tiredness, being killed, taken captive and being wounded. Likewise, through illnesses which afflict a person or which afflict his beloved ones. And you will most certainly hear much abuse from those who were given Scripture before you and from those who associate partners with Allāh, such as reviling you, your religion, your Book and your Messenger. In informing His believing servants of this, there are numerous benefits. From them are: a) That the Exalted’s wisdom necessitates and requires [that they be tested in this manner] so that the true believer can be distinguished from others, b) That the Exalted decrees these affairs upon them because of the goodness He desires for them so that their rank and status will increase, their sins will be expiated, they are increased in faith by it and thereby attain certainty... c) He informed them of this so that they can prepare themselves for its occurrence, to remain patient when it does happen. As such, they would have already prepared for its occurrence and it therefore becomes easier for them to bear it, its burden becoming lighter for them...
3:186.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

3:186.text: Meaning, it is necessary that a believer will be put to trial in something of his wealth, his personal self, his children or his family. And the believer is put to trial to the extent of his religiosity. If he has firmness in his religion his tribulation will be increased. And you will most certainly hear much abuse from those who were given Scripture before you and from those who associate partners with Allāh. The Exalted is saying to the Believers when they came to Madīnah, prior to the Battle of Badr, consoling them over the harm they suffered from the People of the Book and the Polytheists. He ordered them to show indifference, have patience and show forgiveness until Allāh provides them a way out. Hence, He said: But if you patiently persevere and remain devoutly obedient—that will be a determining factor [which you must hold on to with firm resolve].
3:186.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

4:6.text: until they reach marriageable age, meaning [they reach] the level of men and women. If you then observe sound judgement from them, the [Qurʾānic] commentators said: In intelligence, religiosity, safeguarding wealth and knowledge of what is beneficial to him.
4:6.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

4:48.text: This verse is: A refutation of the Muʿtazilah in the subject of [the implementation of the] threat [for sins] and upon the Shurāṭ [the Khārijites] in the subject of [the ruling upon] sins. As for the Muʿtazilah, then they claim that the one who dies upon sins—not having repented from them—will remain eternally in Hellfire. However, Allāh has informed in this verse that from the sinful [believers] who die upon sins without repentance are those He will forgive... And as for the refutation of the Khārijites [Shurāt] regarding the subject of sin, then they consider both the minor and major sin to constitute disbelief (kufr). But if disbelief is disbelief and sin is also disbelief, then what is the thing [mentioned in this verse] that Allāh will forgive after associationism (shirk), for whomever He wills [if sins are also disbelief]?
4:48.author: Al-Imām Muḥammad bin ʿAlī al-Qaṣṣāb (d. 360H)

4:34.text: This verse is referred to as the “wife-beating” verse by Islām haters in their various factions and types. Marriage is a contract between a man and woman wherein the man offers protection, support, shelter, food, clothing, companionship, love, intimacy, care and mercy to a woman (and to the children she bears him). It is through this contract that he makes sexual relations with her lawful. In turn, she offers loyalty and safeguarding of his interests. Therefore, this verse reminds that men, by virtue of: — a) their physical, biological and emotional constitution—which differs from that of women and by which they are protecters and defenders of women, — b) and their toils and struggles in earning and then spending upon their women and other dependents, deserve loyalty, obedience and fidelity from their wives as part of the marriage contract. The verse then provides guidelines for a particular type of woman in which there is recalcitrance, rebelliousness, stubbornness which is wrong and completely out of place, given that the man protects her and provides for her. She has no right to behave in this manner which opens the door for marital discord, sexual misconduct or wastage and destruction of his wealth. For women with such characters, a step by step process is provided for rectification. The first stage is advice, admonition and reminder with gentleness. The second is to display dissatisfaction and displeasure by avoiding intimacy with her. The final stage of this process—after all else fails—is to discipline her in a non-violent, non-harmful way that is more symbolic and psychological in nature than it is physical. This is after reminder, admonition and separating from her by not talking to her and not having intimate relations with her all fail to mend her behaviour. Only a truly rebellious and ungrateful woman would reach this stage. In accordance with the fundamental facts and realities of human nature—since women of this nature can and do exist—Allāh, the Most High, allowed husbands to discipline such women but without harming them or causing them pain, as is established in the Prophetic traditions and explained by the famous Qurʾān commentators such as Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿAṭāʾ, Saʿīd bin Jubayr, al-Shaʿbī and others. As for when violence is used to inflict harm and injury and motivated by revenge and desire to inflict pain or commit abuse then this becomes a criminal offence in Islāmic law. This issue is discussed by Muslim jurists in their works and they state that a woman has the right of divorce if the husband is violent towards her, causing her pain, harm and injury. “When it is established with the judge through clear evidence that the husband harms his wife while she is bonded to him in marriage, even if the harm took place only once, then that which is known [among the jurists] is that she is granted a choice. If she wishes, she can remain [with him] in regards to this situation, and if she wishes, she can divorce herself from him, with a single divorce of severance, due to the [Prophetic] tradition: ‘There is no [causing of] harm and nor reciprocating of harm.’ ... and from what constitutes harm is cutting off speech with her, turning his face away from her, and hitting her, causing her pain thereby.” From Sharḥ Mukhtaṣir Khalīl by al-Khurashī, a work of Mālikī jurisprudence, (Dār al-Fikr, 4/9). Hence, Islāmic law prohibits violence, inflicting harm or pain and commands benevolence, kindness, patience and forbearance with women, and violating these prohibitions have legal ramifications. As for the disciplining of the rebellious woman through non-harmful means, then that is a unique and exceptional circumstance, a matter of last resort. Most women are not inclined to such traits or behaviours. Refer to (4:19:), (2:228:), (2:231:) and also the ḥadīth: “Verily, the best of you are those who are the best to their wives, and I am the best of you towards my wife.” Related by al-Tirmidhī (no. 3895), declared ṣaḥīḥ by Imām al-Albānī. And Imām al-Dārimī presents a chapter titled: “Chapter: Prohibition of Beating Women” in his Sunan within which he cites a few traditions censuring men that beat women. There are many texts present in this regard. As for secular, atheistic, materialistic societies, then domestic violence is at epidemic levels due to a) the promotion of sexual liberation philosophies which produce jealous, covetous, resentful, suspicious, vengeful souls and corrupt and destroy marriage relationships and b) significant consumption of alcohol and other intoxicants and c) turning sport into religion whereby a man will beat his wife just because his team lost, often under the influence of alcohol—and other factors in addition to these few. Devout Muslims are free from all of this because the Islāmic legislation has safeguarded their beneficial interests. This is why domestic violence is extremely rare among devout Muslims who follow the Prophetic guidance with respect to their women: one which commands benevolence, kindness and forbearance with respect to women.

The "beating" in this verse is one of discipline (taʾdīb) and not one of causing harm, for it is this that will rectify her and lead to her fulfil his right... And in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim [is the ḥadīth]: “Fear Allāh with respect to women, for you have taken them upon Allāh’s trust and you have made intercourse lawful with them through the Word of Allāh. Your right over them is that they do not enter those you dislike into your home. If they do so, then discpline them in a non-violent, non-harmful (ghayr mubarriḥ) way.” ... And what is related by al-Tirmidhī who authenticated it from ʿAmr bin al-Aḥwaṣ that he witnessed the farewell pilgrimage with the Messenger of Allāh (صلى الله عليه وسلم). He [the Messenger] praised and extolled Allāh, then reminded and admonished, and then said: “Truly, you should hold the best of intentions for being good towards women, for they are your helpers, and you hold no authority over them in anything other than that. Unless they come with clear, immoral conduct. If they do that, then refuse to lie with them, and discipline them in a non-harmful, non-painful way. But if they return to your obedience, then do not seek a means (of harm or annoyance) against them. Verily, you have rights over your women and your women have rights over you. As for your right over your women, it is that they do not give repose [in your homes] to those whom you dislike, and that they do not grant permission to those whom you dislike to enter your homes. And truly, their right over you is that you are benevolent to them with regards to clothing and food.”
4:34.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

4:34.text: As for what “hit them” means from a physical point of view, then this has been explained by the Prophet’s Companions such as Ibn ʿAbbās and their students, in accordance with the Prophetic traditions that state in a “non-painful, non-harmful way” (ghayr mubarriḥ). ʿAṭā said: “A strike with a siwāk (a natural toothbrush stick with a length and size like that of a child’s toothbrush).” Refer to al-Baghawī and others.

4:54.text: The Jews were envious that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) was allowed multiple wives (for important and strategic reasons connected to his call), and so they criticised him for it. Al-Baghawī said: So whoever interpreted the bounty to mean multiple wives, interpreted the great kingdom regarding David and Solomon (عليهما السلام) to be in relation to many wives. For Solomon had a thousand women, seven-hundred captives and three-hundred free women, and David had a hundred wives. Yet Allāh’s Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم) only had nine wives, so when he said that to them, they (the Jews) went quiet.
4:54.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

4:59.text: Then He ordered with His obedience and obedience to His Messenger. This occurs by fulfilling their commands, both the obligatory and recommended, and avoiding their prohibitions. And He ordered with obedience to those in authority. And they are those with authority over the people from the leaders (ʿumarā), judges (ḥukkām) and scholars who give verdicts (mufṭīs). For the religious and worldly affairs of the people are not set aright except by obedience to them and compliance with them, out of obedience to Allāh, and out of aspiration for what lies with Him [of reward]. But with the condition that they do not command with disobedience to Allāh.
4:59.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

4:59.text: Regarding “those in authority” there are four statements: — The first, that they are the rulers, and this is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Hurayrah, al-Sudī and Ibn Zayd. — The second, that they are the scholars and jurists, and it is the saying of Jābir bin ʿAbd Allāh, al-Ḥasan, ʿAṭāʾ and Abū al-ʿAliyah. — Theyare the companions of Allāh’s Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم), and it is the saying of Mujāhid. — They are Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, and it is the saying of ʿIkrimah.
4:59.author: Al-Māwardī (d. 450H)

4:59.text: Ibn ʿAbbās said: and those in authority over you, “Meaning, the people of understanding and religion.” The same was said by Mujāhid, ʿĀṭāʾ, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and Abū al-ʿĀliyah, and those in authority over you , “Meaning, the scholars.” That which is apparent, and Allāh knows best, is that it is general for all those in authority, whether scholars or rulers, as has preceded.
4:59.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

4:59.text: And this is the most correct [view] that “those in authority” is general to both the scholars and the rulers, even though it is more apparent in relation to the rulers. However, the people of knowledge are also from those in authority in explaining Allāh’s rulings, and explaining what is permissible, what is unlawful and what is lawful. So they are “those in authority” from the angle of explanation. And the rulers are “those in authority” from the angle of affirmation and [implementing] the rulings. Source Audio.
4:59.author: Imām Ibn Bāz (d. 1420H)

4:59.text: Refer also to (4:83:) which is further explanation that those in authority includes the scholars, the people of knowledge, sound opinion and understanding.

The report varies from Imām Aḥmad (رحمه الله تعالى) regarding ‘those in authority’. There are two reports from him (رحمه الله تعالى): The first of them is that they are the scholars. The second is that they are the rulers. And both views are established from the Companions in the explanation of the verse. What is correct is that the verse applies to both groups together. For the scholars and the rulers are those in authority over the affair with which Allāh sent His Messenger. The scholars are its guardians in terms of preservation, explanation, defence of it and refuting the one who swerved and deviated from it.
4:59.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

4:83.text: This is discipline taught by Allāh to His servants about this unbefitting action of theirs. That it is befitting for them—when an important affair and general matter of beneficial interest comes to them, one which relates to security and the happiness of the believers, or which relates to fear in which there is an affliction, that they be firm and not be hasty in spreading the news. Rather, they ought to return it back to the Messenger and those in authority over them, the people of [sound] opinion, and of knowledge, advice, intelligence and composure, those who know the beneficial interests and what opposes them.
4:83.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

4:83.text: From Qatādah: if only they had referred it back to the Messenger and to those in authority over them, “To their scholars.” From Ibn Jurayj: if only they had referred it back to the Messenger so that he can be the one who informs them and to those in authority over them, “To the people with intellect and comprehension in religion.”
4:83.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

4:83.text: The Exalted’s saying: if only they had referred it back to the Messenger and to those in authority over them, meaning, they had not spoken about it [to the people] and did not spread it so that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) would be the one who would speak about it and spread it. Or, “those in authority” [would do so], and they are the people of knowledge and understanding. Al-Qurṭubī goes on to explain the meaning of (الاستنباط), explaining that its linguistic meaning is to extract something out of the earth, or the first water that is extracted out of a well. And here, it means to make ijtihād in the absence of revealed text or consensus pertaining to the matter at hand. Hence, this is the field of the scholars and jurists, in connection with the rulers.
4:83.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

4:136.text: Al-Kalbī “This was revealed regarding ʿAbd Allāh bin Salām, and his brother, Salamah, Yāmin bin Yāmīn, and they are the believers from the People of the Book.”
4:136.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

4:136.text: Those mentioned believed in the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and in Moses and ʿUzayr (Ezra) and the Torah but they denied other books and messengers. So this verse was revealed, commanding them to believe in Allāh, His Messenger, the Qurʾān (which they already did) and also past scripture, including the Injīl (Gospel) of Jesus, the Zabūr of David and others and informing them that to reject any revealed book or sent messenger is disbelief in all of His books and messengers and in Allāh Himself. So they believed in all of the books and messengers.

4:171.text: This verse comprises repudiation, correction and admonition for Jews and Christians who exceeded the limits with respect to Jesus, Son of Mary. The Jews rejected him, reviled him and abused him for pointing out their excesses and deviations. It is written in their books that he was an imposter, a magician and burns in Hell in hot excrement, and that his mother, Mary, was an indecent woman. We seek refuge in Allāh from such calumnies, and may His curse be upon the liars for as long as these calumnies persist. The Christians claimed him to be an incarnation of the Creator, and consider him to be the Lord of the Worlds and they claim that the Lord of the Worlds gave himself up to be killed for atonement of their sins! Allāh explained to both of these recipients of past scripture and exaggerationists that Jesus is but a created servant of His, a Messenger, and that He was created without a father (as a sign for mankind). That he came to be through a word of command, “Be”, delivered by Jibrīl to Mary, and through the blowing of a created spirit into Mary (the same spirit or soul through which all men are given life), without requiring impregnation by a man. The title “Son of Mary”, repeated often in the Qurʾān is a refutation of the Christians who claim he is the”Son of God”, because it is indicative of Jesus not having a father, and not being a “part” of God, and not begotten by Him, but born of a woman through miraculous birth. Just as the title of “Son of Mary”, being an honour for Mary, and the title of “the Messiah” is a refutation of the Jews who having rejected him have never ceased waiting for their own Messiah, (the Dajjāl, the Anti-Christ), and having throughout the ages, been made fools of, misled, deceived and embezzled by multitudes of false messiahs appearing in their midst. And upon that, from the strangest and most contradictory of terms is “Judaeo-Christian”, since they are in polar opposites to each other in relation to Jesus, Son of Mary, and from the strangest of species are those called “Christian Zionists.” Both of these groups are allied with each other against the People of Islām and Tawḥīd, those who believe in Jesus, Son of Mary with the correct, moderate and true belief, and who also believe in all the Prophets and Messengers, and in all past scriptures (in their original forms, prior to adulteration). The Qurʾān is a proof against them and Muslims are witnesses over them. They wish to extinguish the light of Allāh with their mouths, but Allāh will perfect it, even though the disbelievers hate it. (61:8:)

Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said: ( وَرُوحٌ مِنْهُ ) a spirit from Himself, this is what made the Christians fall into misguidance, they said: “Jesus is a part of Him, so they manifested ignorance and went astray, and it has eight responses... And from those he mentions is that this “spirit” is but the created soul through which all men are given life, which is blown into them, and it is mentioned in the Qurʾān annexed to Allāh, to confer superiority and excellence to Jesus (عليه السلام). The ascription of “spirit” to Allāh is like other ascriptions, “Favour of Allāh”, “House of Allāh”, “Messenger of Allāh” and so on. He is also called “Spirit” because Jibrīl blew (النفخ) the created spirit of life into Mary and (النفخ) is but (الريح). Also the meaning of ( رُوحٌ مِنْهُ ) a spirit from Himself is a spirit created from Himself, as we see in the verse (45:13:), about the subjection of what is in the Heavens and the Earth, ( جَمِيعاً مِنْهُ ) all from Himself. It is also said that ( رُوحٌ مِنْهُ ) a spirit from Himself is “mercy from Himself”, as Jesus was a mercy to those who followed him, and it is also as Allāh said ( وَأَيَّدَهُمْ بِرُوحٍ مِنْهُ ) and He aided them with a spirit from Himself (58:22:), meaning mercy from Himself. It is also said: “An evidence (برهان) from Himself,” since Jesus was a proof for his people. All of this and more renders futile the claim of ignorant Christians who claim that this verse contains proof for the divinity of Jesus, this is not understood or said except by a rank ignoramus.

Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said: ( وَكَلِمَتُهُ أَلْقاها إِلى مَرْيَمَ ) and His Word which He delivered to Mary, meaning He was created through the word “Be”, thus he became a man without having a father. The Arabs name a thing with [the name of] another thing when it arose from it. Meaning, Jesus is said to be the “Word of Allāh” because He came to be through the spoken word of Allāh, meaning His command. The misguidance of the Christians is through their erroneous belief that the attribute of Allāh (speech) can leave Him and transmute into a separate entity.

Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said: ( وَكَلِمَتُهُ أَلْقاها إِلى مَرْيَمَ ) and His Word which He delivered to Mary… and it is also said that His Word is Allāh the Exalted’s glad tidings to Mary (عليها السلام) and His message to her upon the tongue of Jibrīl (عليه السلام) and this is His saying ( إِذْ قالَتِ الْمَلائِكَةُ يَا مَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنْهُ ) When the Angels said: “O Mary, verily Allāh gives you glad tidings of a Word from Himself (3:45:). Thus, the Word is the glad tiding delivered to Mary through Jibrīl that she will give birth to he whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus Son of Mary. And is said that “the Word” here is with the meaning of (الآية) “Sign”. Allāh the Exalted said: ( وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِماتِ رَبِّها ) And she [Mary] believed in the signs of her Lord (66:12:). And Jesus had four names: The Messiah, Jesus, a Word and a Spirit.

Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H) said: Ibn Abī Ḥātim said [with his chain of narration] to Shāḍh bin Yaḥyā who said about this verse: ( وَكَلِمَتُهُ أَلْقاها إِلى مَرْيَمَ ) and His Word which He delivered to Mary, “It is not the Word (itself) that became Jesus, but through the Word, Jesus came to be.” And Ibn Kathīr also said: Rather, what is correct it is the Word [of glad tidings] that Jibrīl brought to Mary, and so he blew into her [of the spirit, the soul, through which life is breathed into mankind in the wombs of their mothers] by Allāh’s permission, and through that Jesus (عليه السلام) came to be.

5:33.text: That which is well-known is that this noble verse is about the rulings pertaining to those who cut off the paths (of travel). Those who come to people in the towns and desert regions, plunder their possessions, kill them and spread fear, such that people withhold from travelling (due to fear).
5:33.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

5:33.text: And Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Abū Thawr and the people of opinion (Ahl al-Raʾī) said: The verse was revealed regarding those among the Muslims who came out cutting off the paths (of travel), and striving upon the earth with corruption. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The saying of Mālik is correct. Abū Thawr said, providing evidence for this view: “And in this verse is evidence that it was revealed about [Muslims], besides the people of polytheism. And it is His saying (in the next verse) Except those who repent before you gain power over them (5:34:). And [the scholars of Islām] are united that when the people of polytheism, when they come into our hands and then become Muslims that their blood becomes inviolable. So this shows that the verse was revealed regarding the people of Islām. Al-Qurṭubī proceeds to provide further textual evidence that this view is correct.
5:33.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

5:33.text: ʿAbd al-Malik Marwān wrote to the Companion, Anas bin Mālik (رضي الله عنه), asking him about this verse. So Anas wrote back informing him that this verse was revealed regarding a group known as the ʿUranites, and they were from Jubaylah. Anas said that they apostatised from Islām, killed the shepherd, stole his camels, raped women and spread fear of travelling among people.
5:33.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

5:33.text: Anas said: So Allāh’s Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم) asked Gabriel about the judgement regarding the one who waged war (upon society). He said: “The one who plundered wealth and spread fear of travelling, his hand is cut off for his plunder and his foot for causing fear (of travelling). And whoever killed (a person), then kill him. And whoever killed, spread fear and engaged in rape, then crucify him (after killing him).
5:33.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

5:33.text: From Ibn ʿAbbās (رضي الله عنه) that regarding the highway robbers: If they kill and plunder wealth, they are to be killed and crucified. And if they kill but do not plunder wealth, they are killed but not crucified. And if they plunder wealth and do not kill, their hands and feet are cut from opposite sides. And if they make people fearful of travelling, and did not plunder wealth, they are exiled from the land. And it is also the saying of Qatādaha, al-Awzāʿī, al-Shāfiʿī and the people of opinion, may Allāh have mercy upon them all.
5:33.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

5:41.text: This passage was revealed regarding the Jews who did not abide by the reconstructed Torah and its remnants which they had with them. They would not apply the ruling of the Torah for their elites and nobles who committed adultery, but only a lesser punishment, and for others they would apply it. Also, they would not apply the law of retribution between tribes fairly and did so in a manner that opposed the Torah. They would distort the Torah to these ends. Their rabbis would also take bribes in judgement and swerve from truth and justice knowingly. When they had disputes among themselves, they would come to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), seeking a judgement that would align with their desires and which opposed the Torah that was in their hands. So Allāh exposed their deeds and cautioned the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) from agreeing with them and their desires in these matters. He ordered him to judge by justice, by what He revealed in the Torah of Moses and in the Qurʾān, which confirmed the truth that was in the Torah of Moses.

5:45.text: Ibn Jurayj said: “When [the Jewish tribe of] Qurayḍhah saw that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) had judged with stoning (the adulterer) (in the dispute among themselves), and they tried to hide it in their scripture, the Qurayḍhah rose up and said: ‘O Muḥammad, judge between us and our brothers, Banū Naḍīr.’ There was a blood dispute between them before the arrival of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). The Naḍīr were haughty towards Banū Qurayḍhah, and their blood money was half that of the Nāḍīr. The blood money was a measure (wasq) of dates, 140 measures for Banū al-Naḍīr (if a Naḍīrī was killed) and 70 for Banū Qurayḍhah (if a Quraḍhī was killed). He (the Prophet) said: ‘The blood of a Quraḍhī is equal recompense for the blood of a Nāḍīrī.’ So Banū al-Naḍīr became angry, and said: ‘We will not obey you regarding stoning, but we shall remain upon the limits we were following.’ So Allāh revealed the verse: Then is it the judgment of (the era of) ignorance that they seek (5:50:) and And We ordained for them therein that a life (taken) for a life was revealed.”
5:45.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

5:45.text: Ibn ʿAbbās said: “In what Allāh wrote for Moses in the Torah, there was no blood money for a soul that was killed, or for wound, or a tooth, eye or nose. It was only retribution or pardon.” And he also said: “So why do they disobey, killing two souls for one soul and gouging out two eyes for one eye?”.
5:45.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

5:45.text: This is also from [the affairs] for which the Jews were rebuked and criticised, for in the text of the Torah that is with them it is (stated) “a soul for a soul”, but they deliberately and stubbornly disobeyed it. They stipulate a Naḍrī for a Quraḍhī, but do not stipulate a Quraḍhī for a Naḍrī. Instead, they resort to blood money (in disobedience of the law), just as they disobeyed the ruling of the Torah regarding the stoning of the married adulterer, and they resorted to what they devised themselves of flogging, blackening and humiliating in public (for their elites and nobles).
5:45.author: Imām Ibn Katḥir (d. 774H)

5:46.text: Meaning: We followed [the sending of] those prophets and messengers who judged by the Torah with Our servant and messenger, Jesus son of Mary, the Spirit of Allāh [that was breathed into Mary] and His Word [of command to Jibrīl, through which he was created]. Allāh sent him to confirm what came before him of the Torah, being a witness for Moses and what he came with of the Torah, aiding his call and judging by his legislation (sharīʿah), and being in agreement with him in most of the affairs of legislation, though Jesus (عليه السلام) was more lenient than him in some of the laws.
5:46.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

5:47.text: The Qurʾānioc exegetes explained the meaning of this verse, saying that since every revealed book was revealed to be acted upon, the people who were given the Injīl (Gospel) through Jesus, son of Mary, were commanded and obligated to act upon its guidance and law, to judge by it, and to believe in its reports (regarding the past, future and hereafter), without distorting and altering it, and this includes its prophecies regarding Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم). So just as they were commanded in that time, then they are commanded now also, to judge truthfully by what is in the actual Gospel, the true Gospel, in which they will find the description of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم). This will lead them to belief in Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and the Qurʾān in which there is confirmation of the Torah of Moses and the Gospel of Jesus and clarification of that which they omitted, distorted, altered and added, leading them sound belief, righteous action and just law.

5:51.text: This āyah (verse) and what follows it was revealed in connection with the hypocrites, such as ʿAbd Allāh bin Ubayy bin Salūl. Due to the disease of doubt and hypocrisy in their hearts, they were fearful that the affairs may overturn where Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) suffers defeat and the Jews regain the power that they had prior to Islām, when they used to boast that when their anticipated prophet arrives, the one whose description and location they knew from their scriptures, he will lead them to complete domination over them (the Pagan Arabs). The Jews were strong, they had built fortresses and buildings, they were makers of weapons and were traders, and thus, would have benefited from the wars among the Pagan Arabs. For this reason, the likes of ʿAbd Allāh bin Ubayy, who sought power and leadership, were waiting to see who would be victorious, and hence, displayed faith outwardly while concealing disbelief inwardly for reasons of political and economic expediency. To this end, they maintained allegiance with the Jews of Madīnah (and the Christians of Shām) so that if the affairs turned around, they would not be harmed and be in a favourable position. So these āyāt command the Prophet and the Believers not to be like these hypocrites, for this is a blameworthy trait, to behave in this manner, and also because the Jews are allies of one another, and the Christians are allies of one another. These verses are in the context of strategic alliances in affairs of empire, state, diplomacy and the likes, since a Muslim is otherwise permitted to marry women from the People of the Book, in which there is worldly intimacy, love, friendship and loyalty, and likewise, a Muslim is allowed to eat the meat of the People of the Book,and is also permitted to trade with them. However, alongside that, in what relates to private and sensitive matters of the world and religion, a believer is advised with caution and forbidden from allegiance and intimacy. This is a comprehensible matter, since people of all nations and creeds take a degree of caution and have limits of intimacy and trust towards those who are not of them. In short, Muslims are advised to behave prudently and honourably, unlike the treacherous hypocrites.

5:82.text: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H) said: These two [Jews and Pagans, Polytheists] are the greatest of people, absolutely, in their enmity towards Islām and the Muslims. They are most frequent in striving to bring harm to them. This is because of their severe hatred for them, out of transgression, jealousy, opposition and disbelief. [Regarding the Christians being nearest in affection], the Exalted mentioned numerous reasons for that: From them, among them are priests and monks, meaning, abstemious scholars and worshippers, who are engaged in worship in monasteries. And knowledge comes with abstention [from the world] and likewise, worship is from that which makes the heart gentle and softens it, and removes what it may have of harshness and coarseness. For that reason, you do not find among them, the harshness of the Jews and severity of the polytheists. And among [the reasons] is that they are not arrogant, meaning, they do not have arrogance and nor insolence towards accepting and complying with truth. And this necessitates their nearness to the Muslims and having affection towards them, for the humble one is closer to goodness than the arrogant one.

Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H) said: He did not intend all of the Christians, because they are like the Jews in their killing and capturing of Muslims, destroying their cities, demolishing their mosques and burning their copies [of the Qurʾān]. Rather, the verse is about those who became Muslims among them, such as Negus and his companions. And it has been said that [this verse] was revealed about the Jews as a whole and the Christians as a whole, because the Jews are more hard-hearted and the Christians are more soft-hearted than them and they [the Christians] were lesser in aiding the polytheists [against Muslims] than the Jews. What al-Baghawī (1044- 1122 CE) said in his time—and he was alive in the era of the first crusade in 1096-1099 CE—has truth. For among the Christians are those who have enmity towards Muslims in a like manner to that found among the Jews. In the modern era, this has surfaced in the form of a very strange species known as “Christian Zionists”, who serve the agendas of the Zionist, ethno-supremacist Jews who bomb Palestinian Semitic Arabs, and murder civilian men, women, children, babies and the unborn, and destroy mosques, hospitals, churches, relief shelters and aid organisations—upon the “Amalekite annihilation” bloodthirsty revenge doctrine, which they explicitly invoke. Among the Jews, however, are those who vehemently reject and denounce these actions.

Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H) said: This is because the disbelief of the Jews is [out of] insolence, rejection [upon knowledge of the truth], disdain of the truth, looking down upon people and belittling the carriers of [revealed] knowledge. For this reason, they killed many of the Prophets until they sought to kill the Messenger of Allāh (صلى الله عليه وسلم), and they incited those who resemble them from the polytheists against him. Those who claim they are “Christians”, from the followers of the Christ and upon the way of his Gospel, they have love of Islām and its people in general, and that is only because of what is in their hearts, since they are upon the religion of Christ of mercy and compassion, as the Exalted said: ( وَجَعَلْنَا فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ رَأْفَةً وَرَحْمَةً ) And we placed compassion and mercy in the hearts of those who followed him… (57:27:). In their Book there occurs: “Whoever slapped you on the right cheek, then turn your left cheek to him.” And fighting was not legislated in their religion.

Imām al-Ṭabarī (d.310H) said: Allāh, lofty be His remembrance, has informed about a faction among the Christians whom He praised [Negus and his companions] with respect to their nearness in affection to the people of faith in Allāh and His Messenger. That this occurs from them because they are people of striving in worship and asceticism in monasteries and that among them are scholars, learned in their books and those who rehearse [these books]. Thus, they are not far from the Believers due to their humility towards the truth when they come to know it, they do not show arrogance from accepting it when it is clear to them, because they are people of religion and striving therein, and in being honest [with themselves and each other] in pursuing Allāh’s [pleasure]. They are not like the Jews, those ones who were accustomed to killing the Prophets and Messengers, showing insolent opposition to Allāh in His command and prohibition, and altering His revelation which He sent down in His Books.

Shaykh Ibn ʿUthaymīn (d. 1421H) said: The address in this verse is either to the Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم), and thus the speech about the Jews, Christians and Polytheists in this verse is regarding those in the era of whom? The Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم). Or the address is to everyone… thus these descriptions are general for those [groups] until the Day of Judgement. So the verse can carry [these meanings]. Alongside that, even if we spoke with [the view that the verse is] general, then it is not generalised to every Jew specifically, or every Christian secifically, or every polytheist specifically. Rather, this ruling is from the route of generalistion. The Jews are those who claim they are followers of Moses and they say: “We are the chosen people of Allāh”, they belittle other nations, and they are known for arrogance, seeking highness and haughtiness, until even against their Messenger, Moses (عليه السلام)… they are a faction among Banī Isrāʾīl who claim they follow who? Moses. And those who associate partners [with Allāh], [they are] from the Arabs and other than them. These two groups from the the Sons of Ādam, they are the most severe of people in enmity towards the Believers. As for the Jews, the reason for their enmity is that they envied the Arabs because the general [universal], lasting Messengership was among them. Before that the Jews used to anticipate victory over the people of disbelief [the Pagan Arabs] and would say: “A Prophet will be sent, we will follow hm and will be aided against you.” But when Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم) was sent from among the Arabs, they became jealous and rejected that. As for the Polytheists, then they became the severest of people in enmity because they are opposed to Tawḥīd, whereas the Believers are [pure] Monotheists [in belief, word and deed]. So the polytheist hates the monotheist, dislikes him and sees him as as the greatest enemy to him.

6:74.text: Muḥammad bin Isḥāq, al-Daḥḥāk and al-Kalbī said: “Āzar is the name of the father of Ibrāhīm, who is also Tārakh, similar to Isāʿīl (Israel) and Yaʿqūb (Jacob).” And Muqātil bin Ḥayyān said: “Āzar is the title of Ibrāhīm’s father, his name is Tārakh.”
6:74.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

6:74.text: Al-Thaʿlabī said:“Ibrāhīm’s father’s name that was given to him by his father was Tāraḥ. When he became a keeper for Nimrūd over his gods, he called him Āzar.”
6:74.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

6:152.text: The Exalted’s saying: until he reaches [mental and physical] maturity, meaning his strength (quwwah). This can be in terms of the body, or in terms of knowledge and experience, and it is a must that both aspects are attained. This is because the strength is mentioned here unrestrictedly [without qualification]. [Mention of] the condition of the orphan has [already] come in Sūrah al-Nisāʾ: And test the orphans [in their abilities] until they reach marriageable age (4:6:). Hence, He combined between the strength of the body, which is reaching marriageable age, and the strength of knowledge, when they are perceived to have sound judgement.
6:152.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

6:152.text: Al-Shaʿbī and Mālik said: “( الأَشُدُّ) is having a wet-dream, [after which] good deeds are recorded for him and bad deeds are recorded against him.” And Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: “Until he is able to reason [with sound judgement] and his faculties of strength come together.”
6:152.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

6:152.text: ( الأَشُدُّ) is when the strength of manliness and age become firmly settled until a boy reaches the boundary of [being counted among] men. Editorial Note: And the same applies to girls, it is when they become women when the qualities and experiences that make them women take root in them. And this is not fixed to any time, but to the attainment of the quality described.
6:152.author: Al-Khāzin (d. 725H)

7:96.text: His saying (... وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ ٱلْقُرَىٰٓ) is evidence for drawing down sustenance [from Allāh] through [one's] obedience [to Allāh] and [evidence] for its deprivation on account of sins.
7:96.author: Al-Imām Muḥammad bin ʿAlī al-Qaṣṣāb (d. 360H)

8:25.text: Zaynab bint Jaḥsh J said: “O Messenger of Allāh, will we perish whilst there are the righteous among us?” He said: “Yes, when evil (al-khabath) becomes abundant.” Related by al-Bukhārī (no. 3167) and Muslim (no. 2880). Al-Nawawī commented: “The meaning of the ḥadīth is that when evil increases then a general destruction can take place, even if there are righteous people (among them).” Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (9/257).
The intent of the verse is: Fear the trial which goes beyond the oppressor [on account of whose deeds it befell], such that it afflicts both the righteous and the sinful.”
8:25.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

9:30.text: The Exalted’s saying: And the Jews said is a wording that departs from generalisation and whose meaning is specification because not all the Jews said that. It is similar to the saying of the Exalted Those to whom the people [al-nās] said... (3:173:), however not all people said that, [it was only the hypocrites]. It is said that those who expressed what has been cited from the Jews [of this saying] were Salām ibn Mishkam, Nuʿmān bin Abī Awfā, Shās bin Qays and Mālik bin al-Ṣayf. They said it to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). Al-Naqāsh said: ‘There does not remain any Jew who says it, rather they have died out.’ Note: Various commentators cite that the aforementioned individuals came to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and said to him: “How can we follow you when you have abandoned our qiblah (direction of worship), and you do not hold that ʿUzayr was the son of Allāh, the Exalted.” Thereupon, this verse was revealed.
9:30.author: Al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

9:30.text: Al-Qatādah and al-Suddī said: “The Christians resembled the saying of the Jews before them, and said ‘The Messiah is the son of Allāh’, just as the Jews said, ‘ʿUzayr is the son of Allāh’.” And Mujāhid said: “They resemble the saying of the polytheists before them who used to say that al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and Manāt are the daughters of Allāh.” Al-Ḥasan said: “He resembled their disbelief with the disbelief of the past disbelieving nations.”
9:30.author: Al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

9:30.text: In some of the Old Testament Pseudopigrapha (falsely-ascribed works) such as the Syriac text of 4 Ezra, there exists an account of the ascent of Ezra and his taking on a divine character. The School of Divinity at the University of St. Andrews provides resources on such Pseudopigrapha and notes: In the Syriac text of 4 Ezra 14:48 (and the versions that derive from it) there is a brief account of the ascent and apotheosis of Ezra which is missing in the Latin of 2 Esdras. The Latin text was probably mutilated when 6 Ezra was added onto it. (It would not have made sense to have had additional oracles from Ezra once he had ascended to heaven.) This indicates that there were among the Jews who wrote and ascribed things to Ezra and from the affairs ascribed to him is that he ascended heaven and took on a divine character. The word “apotheosis” means the glorification of a subject to a divine level, to the rank of a god. These Jews remained and some of them were present in al-Madīnah as been indicated above.

This verse is criticised by Jews and Christians alike because they claim: “The Jews do not hold or have never held Ezra to be a ‘son of God’ and then even if they did, it was never in the way Christians hold Jesus as son of God, as this verse incorrectly suggests.” However they are mistaken in their criticisms for the following reasons: 1. There is nothing in the verse that states all the Jews held this view and the definite article in Arabic—as it does in other languages—has numerous applications, only one of which refers to encompassment (of all individuals within the type indicated by the noun). Those who said this in the era of the Prophet have been named in Islāmic sources and they inherited this saying from the Jews who wrote the pseudopigraphical works in the centuries earlier, which they ascribed to Ezra, and which are in the Syriac (Aramaic) language. 2. The resemblance indicated in the verse is from the angle of deification. The polytheists deified their idols and considered them to be the daughters of Allāh, they also held that the angels were daughters of Allāh. Thus, they ascribed angelic and divine status to them. The Jews being alluded to in the verse deified Ezra and considered him to be a son of Allāh, above and beyond what would normally be understood by the term ‘son of Allāh”, which meant a righteous person. They gave him an angelic, divine status. The Christians deified Jesus and considered him to be the “Son of Allāh”. In all three instances, there is deification involved—which is disbelief and a lie that opposes the truth—and in addition to this, they added a familial relationship. This was to indicate more than just righteousness, rather to indicate divinity. 3. It is not possible for Jews and Christians to make critiques and denials of Islāmic texts on the basis of what is or is not present in the canonical books that make up the Bible of the Western Church. This is because they can present no sound criterion or rationale on the basis of which the Christians decided what books were acceptable. As such, the volume and extent of revealed text they claim to possess is not complete. They also ignore the fabrications and lies written by the Jews and Christians which they ascribed to the Prophets. Thus, when the Qurʾān speaks of the Jews and Christians saying words or doing deeds, it is not possible for Jews and Christians to make denials based on complete knowledge.

Reuven Firestone— Professor in Medieval Judaism and Islam at the Hebrew Union College-Jewish Institute of Religion—writes: “The problem presented by this verse was clear to Muslim scholars from the earliest time, because they lived among Jews and therefore observed that Jews did not believe that Ezra was the Son of God. Virtually all of the classical Muslim Qurʾan commentators write that this verse does not refer to all Jews, but rather to certain individuals or groups living in Arabia.” Firestone then cites a report of the four men who came to the Prophet and said they are unable to follow him because he abandoned their direction of prayer and did not accept Ezra as son of God. Then he says: “While it is clear that Judaism as a religious civilization does not accept the view that God has partners or children, it is probable that some fringe groups pushed the limits of acceptable belief with the important figure of Ezra. Two ancient and originally Jewish books, for example, associate a near-divine or angelic status to the biblical personages of Ezra and Enoch. These are 4 Ezra, also known as 2 Esdras 14:9, 50 and 2 Enooch 22:11.” Here Firestone indicates in a footnote that the verse in 4 Ezra exists only in the Syriac, Ethiopic, Armenian and Arabic recensions of the book, but not in Latin. Firestone then says: “Although composed by Jews, both of these books were rejected by Judaism and did not become part of the canonical literature. However, because of their parallels with Christian beliefs, some Christian groups adopted and preserved them. It appears as if some members of a Jewish sect espousing these beliefs were living in Medina at the time of the Prophet and expressed such views, which were immediately rejected and countered through the revelation of the Qurʾanic verse.” Refer to “Children of Abraham: An Introduction to Judaism for Muslims” (Heilbrunn Institute, 2001) pp. 35-36.

What is intended by “the Jews” is the genus of Jews, similar to the Exalted’s saying: Those to whom the people said: “Verily, the people have gathered against you...” (3:173:). He did not say “All of the people” and nor did He say: “Verily, all of the people have gathered against you...” Rather, what is intended is the genus. This is similar to when it is said: “So and so faction does such and such”, and, “The people of such and such [place] do such and such”. So when some of them say it and the others remain silent and do not reject it, then they share in the sinfulness of the statement. Allāh knows best.
9:30.author: Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728H)

9:33.text: His saying (... هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُۥ بِٱلْهُدَىٰ وَدِينِ ٱلْحَقِّ) is a proof for Ahl al-Sunnah against every person from Ahl al-Bidʿah [the people of innovation] who concealed a doctrine... And everyone who is upon something [of doctrine], claiming it is from the religion—whilst he conceals it and does not proclaim it openly—fearing that it will be [refuted and] rejected, then he already knows of its falsehood even before he is asked for its evidence. And in the knowledge of its falsification both the scholar and the ignoramus are equal.
9:33.author: Al-Imām Muḥammad bin ʿAlī al-Qaṣṣāb (d. 360H)

10:93.text: The Jews who believed in Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم), from their learned scholars, included ʿAbd Allāh bin Salām and his family, Muhkhayrīq, Maymūm bin Yāmīn and others. When they recognised that he was the prophet described in their scriptures, they believed in him and in Allāh’s Word, the Qurʾān, which confirmed the Torah of Moses (and the Gospel of Jesus). However, when they became Muslim, the other Jews rejected them and considered them the worst of people, despite affirming them as being the best of them before they became Muslim.

The “honourable place” is said to be the lands of Miṣr (Egypt), Shām (Levant) and Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and its surroundings. When Allāh destroyed Pharoah and his army, the Mosaic state was established over the land of Miṣr (7:137). Then they continued with Moses to seek Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), where the ʿAmāliqah (Amalekites) were settled. However, the Israelites refused to fight against them behind Moses, so Allāh scattered them in the wilderness for forty years. Then Aaron died, and after him, Moses. Then they went out with Joshua, and Allāh gave them conquest over Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). It remained in their power, and they were ruled over by the Prophets David and Solomon. After them, they split into two kingdoms, Israel in the north and Judah in the south. Then, Sargon II of Assyria conquered Israel in 720 BC and Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia conquered Judah in 587 BC and led to the Babylonian exile. Then, the Persians, under Cyrus, conquered Babylon in 539 BC, and the Judeans were allowed to return to Jerusalem. In this period, the seeds of a new religion emerged centred around ethnicity and national identity. Likewise, the Talmudist mindset surfaced during their time in Babylon. It was after their Babylonian captivity and their return to Jerusalem that they (the Israelites and Judeans) became collectively known as the “Jews”. Two hundred years later, the kings of Greece took the land and it was under their rule for a time before it was taken the Romans. In all of these centuries, they were conquered, subdued, separated and punished due to their disbelief, apostasy, sin and transgression. Prophets had been sent to them during this era to admonish them and rectify them, but they paid no heed. They persecuted them, and even killed some of them. Then Allāh sent the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary (عليه السلام) to confirm the Torah of Moses, expunge it of Talmudistry (the “traditions of the elders”), bring ease and give glad tidings. This was not to the liking of those Jewish elders who had put materialism over religion. So they sought help from the authorities in their hostility towards him. They saw him as a threat to the “national identity", lied upon him and convinced the authorities that he would corrupt their subjects. They captured Jesus son of Mary and tried to kill him but Allāh raised him to Himself, and it was made to appear to them that they had killed him. A few decades after the Messiah, when their temple was destroyed by Titus in 70 CE, and later, in the era of Hadrian (132-136 CE), the Jews were exiled and scattered. Many of them began moving westwards and into Europe, mingling and marrying into the nations, while others moved eastwards and some made their way into the Arabian peninsula. From them were the offspring of Joseph and also Aaron, brother of Moses. Three hundred years after the Messiah, Constantine, the Roman Emperor entered the religion of the Christians. He was a philosopher before that and was a believer in Sol Invictus (the myth of the Unconquered Son, the sun god of the Roman Empire). He maintained this belief even after becoming a Christian. Some say that he entered Christianity out of deception, for protection and expansion of empire, and some say his conversion was a ruse to corrupt it. Then Christianity—having been subjected to alteration, distortion, and fabrication—was spread and none remained true to the religion brought by the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, except a small number of ascetics. They established monasteries in remote places, and the pure message of Jesus—worshipping Allāh alone, righteousness, adherence to the law and justification through faith and deeds combined—was lost. Constantine built the city of Constantinople, and he also built churches and large buildings in Bethlehem, Jerusalem, Hawrān and other lands. From that time onwards, they worshipped the cross, praying to the east, they built churches, made pork permissible and other things they have innovated in the foundations and branches of their religion. These Christians—who were formely pagans and idolators—altered the religion of the Messiah and took control of Shām (Levant), Arabia and other places. Jesus the Messiah had informed his followers of a prophet to come, and his descriptions and the place of his emergence was mentioned in the scriptures in the possession of the Jews. Many of them had migrated to the Arabian Ḥijāz in anticipation of this prophet. They thought would be from among themselves (an Israelite, a Jew), and would lead them in conquest against the Pagan Arabs. They had built fortresses and were engaged in commerce. However, when Muḥammad (صلىى الله عليه وسلم) came and he was from the lineage of Ishmael, they rejected him, despite knowing him to be that prophet, just like they knew their own sons (2:146). They worked intrigues, made attempts to assassinate him, and treacherously allied with the Pagans against the Prophet who confirmed the Torah of Moses and the Gospel of Jesus. They had a duty to believe in him and aid him according to their scriptures. However, Allāh made the Prophet (صلىى الله عليه وسلم) victorious, the entire Arabian peninsula became Muslim, and the great nations of the time, the Romans and Persians, already in decline, were also defeated. This land of blessing and honour (Bayt al-Maqdis and Shām in general) was in the hands of the Romans, and they had named it Aelia Capitolina. It was taken (peacefully) by the second caliph, ʿUmar bin al-Khaṭṭāb, and remained in the hands of the Muslims from that time. Jews and Christians lived under Muslim rule through the centuries, their churches and synagogues remained intact, and they lived in relative ease and comfort. However, during the same time in Europe, the Jews who had migrated there were persecuted by the Christians because in their view, they Jews had killed their god (Jesus), and were accused of subterfuge and corruption through usury, sorcery and immorality. After the passing of centuries, the Christians sought a solution to the problem of the Jews, who, by this time, had been expelled repeatedly from many nations. A Christian Zionist movement took shape, which, in part, embodied the desire of European Christians to get the unwanted Jews out of their countries, and in part, sought the fulfilment of prophecy, the Second Coming of Christ. Then in the late 19th century, secular Jews founded the Zionist movement, advocating for Jews to become a nation state. European Jews began to migrate and settle in the land of Palestine in small numbers. Immigration and settlement of mainly Askhenazi Jews from European countries (Poland, Ukraine, Hungary) increased over time, eventually leading to violence and large-scale displacement of Arab Semites who trace back to the Canaanites. Most religious Jews were anti-Zionist, because they saw it as a secular movement attempting to take Jews away from religion to make them a nation like other modern, secular nations. However, by the end of the 20th century, the Zionists managed to capture the majority of World Jewry, both religious and secular, while the rest remained “Assimilationist Jews”. Wealthy Jews engineered a large support base of Christian Zionism through the Scofield Bible which provided a new framework for interpreting the Bible, and captured fundamentalist Christians in the United States. The Zionists derive their political and military power through the indoctrination of Christians in the United States, who have been turned into sympathizers and footsoldiers for Middle-eastern wars. The First World War had led to the demise and break-up of the Ottoman empire, the handing of Palestine to the Rothschilds, and attempts at a worldwide Bolshevik Revolution beyond Russia, which ultimately failed. The victory of International Jewry in the Second World War, which ended a particular European nation’s resistance against Bolshevism (Communism) and its escape from the clutches of international finance and usury, led to the creation of the Jewish state alongside numerous international organisations, such as the United Nations. The aim of such organisations is to consume and dissolve all nations and races through Collectivism (Communism), leaving only the envisaged Jewish ethno-state as the seat of world power. There has been strong collaboration between the Christian and Jewish Zionists and Western nation-states beholden to the Zionist cause to take possession of Jerusalem, the land of Palestine and surrounding areas through political subterfuge, mililtary means (war, terrorism) and ethnic cleansing. Deep underlying religious sentiments and economic and geopolitical interests drive these groups in pursuing their agendas in the region which is made up of Muslim nations. Wealthy, elite Jews foster and manipulate the Christian guilt-complex for the centuries of persecution the Jews suffered in Europe, and propagandise them with the claim that the Muslims (who offered the Jews sanctuary in North Africa and the Ottoman empire from Christian persecution) are their greatest enemies who are set on destroying them. To this end, they engineered a “Clash of Civilisations” and “Islamic Terrorism” narrative to align the Christian West against the Muslim Middle-East, and use the military might of these nations (through finance, political lobbying and blackmail) to support their goal of taking the rest of the land and establishing Greater Israel, in anticipation of their Messiah. However, there are factions of Jews who reject the Jewish state, and claim that they must remain in exile until their awaited Messiah arrives, through whose leadership, they will dominate the nations.

11:112.text: He, the Exalted commands His Messenger and His believing servants with firmness and persistence upon uprightness (istiqāmah). This being from the greatest means of support for [acquiring] help against the enemies and [against the] opposition of adversaries. And [at the same time] He prohibited against oppression, which is transgression (baghy)—even if was against a polytheist—for [such oppression] is a stumbling block [in the acquisition of help]. And then He, the Exalted, informed that He is all-Seeing of the actions of the servants. Editorial Note: Upon what Ibn Kathīr has explained, it is prohibited to oppress an adversary or enemy since doing so is an impediment to the support and aid that is otherwise acquired through uprightness and steadfastness on the path of truth, despite hindrance and oppression from that adversary or enemy. And this indicates the justice and restraint with which Muslims have been commanded.
11:112.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

10:94.text: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and Qatādah said: Meaning, those who believed from the People of the Book, such as ʿAbd Allāh bin Sallām and his associates, they testify to the truthfulness of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and will inform you about his prophethood. Al-Farrāʾ said: Allāh the Sublime knew that His Messenger is not doubtful, but He mentioned this in the habitual usage of the Arabs, where one of them says: “If you are my son, do such and such”, that is not from the angle of doubt.
10:94.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

10:94.text: Though the address is to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) it is directed towards others. Meaning, that you are not in doubt, but others have doubted. “If you are in doubt”, meaning: “Say O Muḥammad, to the disbeliever: So if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who reading the Scripture that came before you.” Meaning: “O worshipper of idols, if you are in doubt about the Qurʾān, then ask those who became Muslim from among the Jews”, meaning, ʿAbd Allāh bin Salām and his likes. This is because the worshippers of idols affirmed that the Jews were more knowledgeable than them because they are people of a (revealed) book. So the Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم) invited them to ask those whom they affirm are more knowledgeable than them.
10:94.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

10:94.text: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H) said: Alongside this knowledge, they know him from their books like they know their own sons, but they confuse, distort and alter it, and do not believe in him despite the proof being established against them. From the Jews were those who were truthful and believed, due to their firm knowledge that this was the prophet mentioned in their scripture, and they had been anticipating him. So they recognised his descriptions and traits and believed in him. And as for those who doubted, whether from the Pagans or from the disbelievers among the People of the Book, then the address in this āyah is directed towards them, for them to return to the truthful, honest and most learned of them, such as ʿAbd Allāh bin Salām, who were learned scholars.

Some Christians claim that this āyah is proof for their scripture and that if their scripture opposes the Qurʾān, then this āyah proves that their scripture is correct and the Qurʾān is wrong. However, this āyah simply confirms that in the remains of scripture in the hands of the Jews and Christians at that time, they had sufficient evidence regarding Muḥammad’s prophethood and the truthfulness of the Qurʾān. The Prophet’s message was the same as that of Abraham, Moses and Jesus, it calls to worshipping Allāh alone, belief in resurrection and recompense, and working righteous deeds and observing the law to attain salvation in the hereafter. This āyah informs that if they are in doubt, they should ask the truthful and learned who read the scripture truthfully, and followed it when it obligated them to believe in and support the prophet that they were expecting.
