Their scriptures mention that there will be a prophet from the offspring of Abraham through Ishmael, through Kedar, and he will appear in the Arabian Hijāz with a new hymn (recital, qurʾān), and he will be opposed by his people, though he will be victorious over them. So the learned ones among the Jews, such as ʿAbd Allāh bin Salām and Mukhayrīq.

11:117.text: The Exalted’s saying: And your Lord would never destroy the townships, meaning the inhabitants of the townships on account of oppression, meaning, through their associationism and disbelief whilst their people were rectifiers, meaning, with respect to fulfilling the mutual rights they have upon each other. Meaning, that He would not destroy them on account of disbelief alone until they add corruption to it. Just like He destroyed the people of Shuʿayb due to greed in giving due measure in the scales (i.e. cheating in trade dealings) and the people of Lot for sodomy. This indicates that sins are closer to the punishment of extermination in this world than associationism (shirk) [on its own], even if the punishment for associationism is more difficult in the hereafter.
11:117.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

11:117.text: Meaning, Allāh would never destroy the inhabitants of the townships by being oppressive towards them, whilst they are rectifiers. Meaning, that they are established upon rectitude, continuing upon it. So Allāh would not punish them [whilst the situation is like this], except when they commit oppression and the proof is established upon them. It can also mean: Your Lord would never destroy the townships on account of their prior wrongdoing, when they return and rectify their actions. For Allāh will pardon them and wipe away the oppression that preceded from them.
11:117.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

11:117.text: And your Lord would never destroy the townships on account of oppression, meaning, He will not destroy them for their associationism (shirk), whilst their people were rectifiers, with respect to their [dealings] between themselves, when they abide by justice with respect to each other, without oppressing one another. Indeed, He destroys them when they engage in oppression towards each other. And it is said: He does not destroy them through oppression on His behalf whilst they are rectifiers in their actions. However, He destroys them because of their disbelief and engaging in sins.
11:117.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

13:39.text: Imām al-Māwardī (d. 450H) provides numerous explanations from the Salaf for this verse and they include: — From Ibn ʿAbbās: Allāh erases or alters the affairs of His servants except happiness and wretchedness (in the Hereafter), for they do not change. Also from Ibn ʿAbbās: That a man follows a good deed with an evil one and hence it erases it or he follows an evil deed with a good one and hence it erases it. — From ʿIkrimah: Allāh erases and affirms whatever He wills in any book besides the Umm al-Kitāb (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ, the Preserved Tablet). — From Qatādah and Ibn Zayd: Allāh abrogates whatever He wills of the rulings of His Book and affirms whatever He wills, without abrogating it. — From al-Ḥasan: That Allāh erases (from the Book) he whose lifespan has come to an end but affirms (in the Book) he whose time has not come. — From Saʿīd bin Jubayr: That Allāh forgives what He wills from the sins of His servants and leaves what He wills, without forgiving it. — From al-Ḍahhāk: That the Angels raise up all of his statements and actions, then Allāh erases those in which there is neither reward nor punishment and affirms those in which there is reward and punishment.
13:39.author: Imām al-Māwardī (d. 450H)

13:39.text: Saʿīd bin Jubayr and Qatādah said that Allāh erases whatever He wills from the legislated acts and obligations. He abrogates them and replaces them (with something else). And He affirms whatever He wills from them, without abrogating them.
13:39.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

13:39.text: In some reports there occurs that a man who has thirty years of his life left, cuts off the ties of kinship and as a result, his lifespan is cut short to only three days. And a man who has three days left, maintains the ties of kinship and it is extended to thirty years... And ʿAṭiyyah relates from Ibn ʿAbbās: It is regarding a man who acts in obedience to Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, and then he returns to disobedience and dies upon misguidance. He is the one who is erased. And the man who acts in obedience to Allāh and dies whilst in obedience to Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, he is the one who is affirmed.
13:39.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

13:39.text: Allāh erases what He wills of the decrees and affirms whatever He wills of them. This erasure and alteration is in relation to other than what Has preceded in His knowledge and what Has been written by His pen. For no replacement or alteration takes place in [His knowledge and writing] because that is impossible upon Allāh—that a deficiency or flaw should arise in His knowledge [is impossible]. Hence, He said And with Him is the Mother of the Book. Meaning, the Preserved Tablet to which all things are referred back to. It is the foundation of all things, whilst all the other [forms of knowledge and writing] are branches and divisions [from that foundation]. The alteration and replacement occurs in these branches and divisions such as the actions of the day and night written by the Angels. Allāh has made causes for their erasure and causes for their affirmation. And these causes do not go beyond what is inscribed in the Preserved Tablet. [As an explanation], Allāh has made righteousness, keeping ties of kinship and benevolence to be the means of a long life and plentiful sustenance. And He made sins to be a means of removal of the blessing of sustenance and life. And He made certain means of deliverance from calamities and destruction to be a cause of safety and made exposure to those causes a means of destruction. Thus, He is the One who controls and regulates the affairs according to His power and wish. And whatever He regulates never opposes what He already knew and wrote in the Preserved Tablet.
13:39.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

13:39.text: In explanation of the above: In the Umm al-Kitāb (the Preserved Tablet), which is the foundation, all affairs are written down, inclusive of all cause-effect systems within Allāh’s creation—whether kawniyy (relating to the elements, forces and nature) or sharʿiyy (relating to legislated deeds). And this Book is from the all-inclusive and all-encompassing knowledge of Allāh. Thus, within this Book for example is that so and so will do such deeds (both worldly and religious) that will prolong his life and lead him to die at a particular moment. This will include not living dangerously, not taking risks, eating well, maintaining good lifestyle habits, being righteous, kind, maintaining ties of kinship and so on. Every time this individual performed each of these actions, then in accordance with the qadariyy and sharʿiyy cause and effect systems that Allāh has created His creation upon—from His knowledge, wisdom and power—then this person’s lifespan increases, in accordance with the decree of Allāh. However, outside of this foundational Book, there are the yearly, daily and lifespan decrees which are in the knowledge and writing of the Angels. These are all temporary, conditional decrees—tied to the kawniyy and sharʿiyy cause effect systems of which Allāh alone has all-encompassing, all-inclusive knowledge, and which are in the Mother of the Book. So these other “branches” from the foundational Book can be subjected to change and replacement due to the effect of the cause effect systems upon them.

16:67.text: And the Exalted put benefits and advantages for His servants in the fruits of date-palms and vines in the form of various types of sustenance that are eaten, fresh and ripe, whether immediate, or stored [for later consumption]. Likewise, food and drink that is derived from its juice as well as wine and intoxicant which used to be lawful previously. Then Allāh abrogated the lawfulness of intoxicants and substituted wholesome, [non-intoxicating] drinks in place of them and various types of permissible delicious drinks. Indeed in that is a sign for a people of reason [who understand] about Allāh and the perfection of His creative decree in that He draws out [these provisions] from trees resembling firewood which turn into delicious and wholesome fruits. And [these are signs] of His all-inclusive mercy in that He made [these favours] to encompass all of his servants, and facilitated [these favours] for them. [And these are signs] that He alone is the true deity, in that He is unique in [the bestowal of these favours].
16:67.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

16:68.text: What is meant by waḥī here is inspiration, guidance and direction for bees to take homes among mountains that they return to and among trees and structures that men build. The bee is precise, with the extremity of precision, in its hexagonal, compact design [of its home] whereby there are no flaws in [the construction of] its home.
16:68.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

16:68.text: Then consider the bees in their various behaviours and what they comprise of signs and admonitions. Observe it and its exertion in manufacturing honey and constructing hexagonal homes which are the most complete of structures, the best of them in roundness, and the most precise of them in construction. When these [hexagonal forms] are put next to each other, there is no gap or flaw between them. And all of this is without any measuring instrument or compass (divider). And that is from the effects of the creation of Allāh, and His inspiring [the bee] and instilling it [with such behaviours].
16:68.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

16:68.text: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H) wrote: Then they embark to build their houses in equal rows, as if they are roads and [lanes of] buildings. They build their houses as hexagons of equal sides, as if they had read the book of Euclid [on Geometry] and came to know the best of shapes for their homes. Ibn al-Qayyim goes on to explain that hexagonal shapes do not leave any gaps and as more and more are added, a circular shape is formed. The particular type of structure created thereby prevents other animals from entering the home of the bee. The bee must know that the only shape which can fill a space without gaps and without narrow corners or corners that are too wide is the hexagon. This cannot be achieved by the triangle, square, pentagon, septagon, octagon and so on. This is evidence of inspiration (programming and guidance) from a Creator from whom such knowledge has been embedded into this amazing creature. Hence, the mere existence of the bee and its activities is direct empirical evidence of His existence and His knowledge, will, creative power and wisdom.
16:68.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

16:69.text: In the creation of this small bee, which Allāh guided through this amazing guidance and facilitated for it the various pastures [to seek its sustenance], and to return to its home which it prepares in accordance with how Allāh taught and guided it to do so, and thereafter, this delicious honey comes out of its belly which is of varying colours depending on the earth and pasture, and in which there is a healing for men for various diseases—all of this is evidence for the perfection in Allāh the Exalted's providence and the completion of His brilliance in His kindness to His servants, and that none besides Him is worthy of being loved [with the love of worship] and being invoked [for one's needs].
16:69.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

17:7.text: If you do good, you do good for your ownselves because benefit will return to you, even in this world [before the hereafter] as you witnessed when he aided you against your enemies. And if you do evil, then it is [to your ownselves], meaning, the harm will return upon yourselves, as Allāh showed you by empowering the enemies [against you]. Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H) Added by: abuiyaad on 10-Jan-19
17:7.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

17:8.text: Within these verses (17:7:) (17:8:) is a warning to this nation from committing acts of disobedience lest what afflicted the Children of Israel afflict them as well. The sunnah (way, rule) of Allāh is one, it does not change or become altered. Whoever looks [and reflects] upon the empowerment of the disbelievers and oppressors over the Muslims will come to know that this was due to their sins, as a punishment to them. [And also to make them realise] that if they enact and establish the Book of Allāh and the Sunnah of His Messenger, He will grant them firm authority in the land and aid them against their enemies.
17:8.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

18:86.text: He traversed a path until he reached the furthest that can be traversed in a westerly direction on the earth, which is the ‘west’ (maghrib) of the earth. As for reaching the west of the sun in the sky, then it is not possible... and as for his saying: he perceived it setting over a hot, muddy spring, meaning that he saw the sun in the vision of his eyes setting in the ocean. And this is the case with everyone who comes to the coast [of the ocean]. He sees the sun as it it is setting over it whereas [in reality] it never leaves its orbit in which it is firmly fixed, without separating from it.
18:86.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

18:86.text: Until he saw the sun in the vision of the eye (marʾā al-ʿayn) as if it were setting over a hot, muddy spring. And this is what is normally seen by the person who stands in a place where there is [an expanse] of water between him and the sun in the western horizon. He will see it setting into the water even though it is high in elevation.
18:86.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (1376H)

18:86.text: Citing Al-Qaffāl: 'The intent is that he reached the furthermost inhabitation in the direction of the west and the direction of the east, and [in the west] he saw it in the vision of the eye (raʾy al-ʿayn) setting over the hot spring, just as we observe it on the plain earth, as if it is entering into the earth. And hence, He said he found it rising over a people for whom We had not made against it any shield (18:90). He did not intend that it rises over them in the sense that it touches them. Rather, he intended that they are the first [of the people of the earth] over whom it rises.' Al-Qutbī said: ‘It is permissible that this spring be in the ocean itself, and it is permissible that the sun disappears into the west behind it or by it or alongside it, and hence [the spring is to the ocean] as an attribute is to a person’. . Editorial note: Meaning that instead of saying “ocean” in the verse, “spring” was used because in the language, an entity can be referred to by its attribute. And in this case, the volcanic spring is an attribute of the ocean, and what is intended is the ocean.
18:86.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

18:86.text: The intent [in this verse] is that he perceived it in the vision of his eye... and this is when the seafarer sees [the sun] as if it rises out of the sea and disappears into it when he does not see any coastline [in front of him]. And the one who is on an expansive, flat piece of land will also see it as if it is rising out of the earth and disappearing into it... Thereafter, the intent behind (حَمِئَة) is either a spring within the ocean, or the ocean itself and there is no issue in [the ocean] being named a “spring” (عَيْن) because it is like a drop in relation to the greatness of Allāh the Exalted, even if it is large in relation to us. Some of the Baghdādī grammarians asserted that (فِي) means “next to” (عِنْدَ), which means that it set [over the horizon] beside a spring... And the sun—according to what is the truth—never ceases to be moving, rising over one people whilst setting over another people, according to their horizons.
18:86.author: Maḥmūd Shukri al-Alūsī (d. 1270H)

18:86.text: Editorial Note: This verse is attacked by non-Muslims and apostates from Islām. However, there is nothing in the verse that opposes what has been and can be observed in reality. As for Dhul-Qarnayn coming across a people in the easternmost part of the earth who had no cover from the sun (18:90:), then this can be envisaged in a hot, desert climate where the land does not have many trees or rocks to provide cover and which is the part of the earth that first sees the sun approach. An example of such an environment could be Australia where for hundreds miles there is nothing but plain land, without much protection from the sun. As for the westernmost part of the earth, then this is the ocean in which there are volcanic eruptions leading to hot, muddy springs in the ocean, over which the sun can be seen to set in the vision of the eye from or near to the coast. An example of such an environment could be the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Chile which is part of the “Ring of Fire”. In addition, there are two readings, one with the word (حَمِئَة), which means muddy, dark and the other (حَامِئَة) which means hot. This is a clear indication to a volcanic spring. One can easily search for “underwater active volcano” to find footage of this phenomena wherein a boiling hot and dark muddy spring is produced in the ocean itself. Further, the verb (غَرَبَ) means to disappear into the west and the preposition (فِي) is used with the meaning of “over” (عَلَى) and this is well-known in the language of the Qurʾān and of the Arabs. As for the verb (وَجَدَ) then it means to perceive with the senses and also to come across, to find, to stumble upon something. In this verse, the verb is used with both these meanings, just as we find in other places in the Qurʾān, where a verb is employed with its numerous meanings. For example, the verb (نَسِيَ) which means to forget, be heedless—which is blameworthy and a shortcoming—and also to deliberately abandon, is used in (45:34:) with both meanings. Allāh abandons those who forgot Him and were heedless of their duty in this life, and for both of these actions, the same verb is used. Hence, in this verse, given what has preceded, it can be envisaged that Dhul-Qarnayn perceived (وَجَدَ) the sun setting over a hot spring in the ocean from a place near to the coast and near it, he came across (وَجَدَ) a people who were polytheists. Thus, the meaning is that Dhul-Qarnayn saw—due to the laws of perspective of vision—the sun setting over and into a hot spring, with the meaning of beyond and behind it, going westwards. And near this location he came across a people. In short, the Qurʾān hints at these locations through descriptions without mentioning place names, since place names are not always fixed and can change over time.

In light of the commentaries above, the following video is a good illustration of how a hot, muddy spring can exist in the ocean, and by the laws of perspective, the sun can appear to set over this type of spring as viewed from a nearby coast-land, the while it remains high in its orbit. Your browser does not support the video tag. The Muslim scholars have stated that the location alluded to in the verse is in the furthest inhabited place in the western part of the earth, and from the description, it is clear that the spring is connected to volcanic activity (hot, muddy) because the verse is read both as ḥamiʾah (muddy, dark) and ḥāmiʾah (hot, boiling) as is related from the Companions. As such, there is nothing in the verse that is outside of what is or has been observable on the earth or is possible to observe on earth. As for the atheists, apostates and Christians who claim that this verse is stating that the sun sets into—as in, physically enters—a hot spring, next to which there are found a people, then this is an indication of their deficiency in intellect or lack of it. First, this would mean that the sun rises from the very same place that it set and upon the very same people, coming out of the same hot, muddy spring. Second , in the verses that follow, Dhul-Qarnayn journeys to another place, to the furthest place east, where the sun first rises upon civilisation. Third, in many other verses, the orbits of the sun, moon and stars in the heaven are mentioned and Muslim scholars explained the phenomena that has been known all people who have ever lived on the coast, that the setting of these celestial bodies is over and into the ocean from the perspective of vision. Fourth, even if one said, “the sun sets into the ocean”, then anyone who sees the phenomena clearly understands what is meant, it is from the perspective of vision. And if it is said, “Zayd, who lives on the coast, sees the sun setting into the ocean every day”, then that is similar to what the Qurʾān states with respect to Dhul-Qarnayn, upon what the commentators have explained. Fifth, the very fact that we say “the sun sets” indicates that we are speaking in terms of the perspective of vision, in terms of what we see. The sun never “sets” at all in actual reality, but we use language that contradicts this reality. Thus, saying “the sun sets into the ocean” and “the sun sets” are both equivalent. Rejecting that the first can be said requires rejecting that the second can be said at all. However, all people understand what is meant when it is said, “the sun sets”—it is from the perspective of vision.

18:90.text: Al-Qatādah and al-Ḥasan said: ‘There was no cover [of protection] between them and the sun and this is because they were in a place in which construction [of an abode] was not possible. So they would be in underground shelters they had made. When the sun passed its zenith (afternoon), they then came out to pursue their livelihood.’ And al-Ḥasan said: When the sun rose [to its zenith] they would enter the water and when it passed over, they would come out and wander around [in search of food] as the animals do.’ Al-Kalbī said: ‘They were a naked people, who would elongate one of their ears and tie the other one.’
18:90.author: Imām a-Baghawī (d. 516H)

18:90.text: What is intended by the rising place and setting place of the sun is the start of habitation [in the furthest place east] and its end [in the furthest place west]. he found it rising over a people for whom We had not made against it any shield, meaning [a shield] that covers them from the sun of buildings, trees and clothes. They would find refuge to burrows they had dug when it rose over them. And when it passed its zenith, they would emerge again to hunt for animals and fish.
18:90.author: Al-Māwardī (d. 450H)

18:90.text: There are two sayings regarding it: The first is that there was no tree, mountain or buildings that would prevent the sun’s rays [of intense heat] fom them. Due to this reason, when the sun rose, they entered into deep burrows in the earth, or they submerged themselves in water. Hence, they were unable to pursue their livelihood as the sun rose and passed over its zenith. But when it departed to the west [in the late afternoon], they became engaged in pursuing the affairs important to their subsistence. Hence, their [pattern of life] was different to that of the rest of the people. And the second saying is that they had no clothing, and they lived completely naked as do the rest of the animals.
18:90.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

18:90.text: Refer also to (18:86:) for further related commentary.

19:65.text: This is an evidence that worship (ʿibādah) is burdensome and tiring. The believer is commanded to have patience in performing it because the label of ṣabr (patience) is not [applied to anything] except that it is tied to aversion and difficulty.
19:65.author: Al-Imām Muḥammad bin ʿAlī al-Qaṣṣāb (d. 360H)

19:65.text: Tawḥīd divides into three types: a) Tawḥīd al-Rubūbiyyah, Tawḥīd al-Ulūhiyyah and Tawḥīd al-Asmāʾ wal-Ṣifāt. And they have come together in the Exalted’s saying Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him alone and remain constant and patient in His worship. Do you know of any that is similar to Him [and worthy of His name]?
19:65.author: Shaykh Muḥammad bin Ṣāliḥ al-ʿUthaymīn (d. 1421H)
19:65.reference: Al-Qawl al-Mufīd (1423H, Dammām: Dār Ibn al-Jawzī) 1/9

21:7.text: [This is] a proof for the acceptance of the solitary nation (khabar al-wāḥid). This is because each one who is asked will inform about that [which he knows] through himself alone. And the proof is binding upon the one being informed through the saying [of the one who is asked].
21:7.author: Al-Imām Muḥammad bin ʿAlī al-Qaṣṣāb (d. 360H)

23:14.text: Regarding So blessed by Allāh, the Best of creators: Some people held that this word should be negated from people because ‘creation’ is ascribed to Allāh, the Exalted. Ibn Juraij said: ‘He said the Best of creators because He the Exalted permitted Jesus—peace be upon him—to create’ and some of them were confused by that. [However], the word [creating] is not negated from humanity upon the meaning of manufacturing (الصنع). Rather, this word (creating) is only negated from them with the meaning of inventing (الختراع) and bringing into existence (الإيجاد) from nothing.
23:14.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

23:14.text: Editorial Note: The world creating (الخلق) has numerous meanings and they include: a) manufacturing, producing (الصنع), in the sense of taking raw materials and producing something out of them, b) determining, defining, specifying (التقدير) the shape, form, attributes and qualities of a thing and c) creating out of nothing (الخلق من العدم). In this verse, the plural form “creators” is used ( الْخَالِقِينَ ), because man was created by Allāh from prior material, just as men create things from prior material. So from this angle, the word ‘create’ can be used for men, without that implying that they create from nothing or are equal to Allāh in their powers of creating. The use of the word (خلق) in the language of the Arabs for the first two meanings is well known, and it is said, (رجل خالق), meaning (صانع) “a manufacturer” and (خلق النعل), “He made shoes” and so on.

Mujāhid said: ‘They make (يصنعون) and Allāh too makes (يصنع), but Allāh is the best of makers (الصانعين).’ The most correct of the sayings is the saying of Mujāhid because the Arabs call every maker, manufacturer (صانع) a ‘creator’ (خالق).
23:14.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

23:14.text: Muqātil said: ‘The Exalted says that He is better in creation than those who create idols and their likes, those which are unable to move.’ Editorial Note: And in a modern context, those who try to mimic biology to solve problems and find solutions for humanity—[through the biotechnology science of biomimicry]—then they are unable to replicate the like of what Allāh has created, in its beauty, precision and efficiency. Rather they can only mimic and produce what is inferior, even if it serves a purpose among the purposes for them.
23:14.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 741H)

23:14.text: Editorial Note: This is among the verses used by Evangelical Christians to justify their ascription of rubūbiyyah (lordship) and ulūhiyyah (divinity that necessitates worship) to Jesus. Being unable to validate their doctrines through their distorted and abrogated scripture in the course of disputing with Muslims, they have turned to the Islāmic texts, in order to distort and misinterpret them for the same purpose. These Christians seek to confuse uninformed and ignorant Muslims who have not received a sufficient education in Islāmic creed and the Arabic language. The argument here is that Allāh has affirmed multiple creators alongside Himself, hence the Qurʾān affirms multiple deities, and as such, there is nothing wrong in our belief of Jesus being Lord. From the citations presented, one can see through the ignorance and sophistry in this doubt. The Muslim scholars such as Ibn Khuzaymah (d. 311H), Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728H), Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H) and many others have explained that there are names and attributes common to Allāh and His creatures such as hearing, seeing, inheriting, guiding, creating and so on. However, there are aspects of the meanings of these words that apply only to Allāh’s attributes and likewise the realities of these attributes are unlike those of the creation, which are imperfect and deficient in their nature and scope. This is a firmly established principle of Ahl al-Sunnah—the people of orthodoxy—in the subject of Allāh’s names and attributes. Educated, informed Muslims will but laugh at these poor souls for their foolishness whilst also invoking Allāh to guide them, out of mercy and pity for them.

25:33.text: He [Allāh] says: If we had revealed the Qurʾān upon you all in one go, then they asked you, you would not have with you what you could answer it with. However, we keep that [revelation] from you and when they ask you, you can then respond. Al-Nuḥās said: “This was a sign of his prophethood because they never asked him anything except that they were given a response about it…” And if it had been revealed all at one with all that it contains of the obligations, it would have been heavy upon them, and Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, knew that rectification lies in revealing it gradually, bit by bit, so that they can be notified again and again. If it had come down all in one go, then the aspect of notification and the aspect of the abrogating and abrogated would have ceased… and it would be impossible for it to be revealed all in one go [wherein they are commanded]: “Do this, and do not do this” [at the same time].
25:33.author: Imām al-Qurṭūbī (d. 671H)

25:44.text: He resembled most people with cattle, and what combines the two types together is that they are alike in not accepting guidance and complying with it. And He [also] declared most people to be more astray than the cattle because the animal is guided by its owner and so it receives direction and follows the path [shown to it], without turning away to the right or left. [In contrast], most people who are invited by the Messengers and guided to the path do not respond. They do not receive guidance and nor do they distinguish between what harms them and benefits them. As for the cattle, then they distinguish between what harms them of vegetation and paths, so they avoid them. And as for what benefits them, then they choose it. Allāh did not create hearts for cattle with which they understand and tongues with which they speak. However, he gave these faculties to these [who are most of the people], but they did not benefit from the intellects, hearts, tongues, hearing and sight [that He bestowed upon them]. Thus, they are more astray than cattle.
25:44.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

28:88.text: The meaning of Everything except His Face is differed upon. So some of them said its meaning is that everything will perish except Him. And others said that its meaning is [everything will perish] except that by which His Face was sought [of righteous deeds].
28:88.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

28:88.text: Everything except His Face will perish, meaning, except Him. And (وَجْهَهُ) is in the accusative sense to signify exception, as if He said: 'Except Him'. ʿĀṭāʾ said: ‘Its meaning is that everything will perish except that by which His Face is sought, and every action done for [the sake of] others besides Him will perish, except what was for Him’.
28:88.author: Imām al-Ṭabarānī (d. 360H)

28:88.text: Everything except His Face will perish, Mujāhid said: ‘Its meaning is : Except Him.’ Al-Ṣādiq said: ‘[Except] His religion.’ Abū al-ʿĀliyah and Sufyān said: ‘Meaning, except that by which His Face is sought’, meaning that by which nearness to Him is intended.”
28:88.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

28:88.text: His saying Everything except His Face will perish informs that He is the Remaining, Everlasting One, the Ever-Living, Self-Subsisting One through whom all others subsist, the One who does not die whereas all others die. Hence, He used the expresssion of “face” to refer to the essence of His being, meaning “Except Him”. Mujāhid and al-Thawrī said: “Everything except His Face will perish, except that by which His Face is sought.” And this saying does not negate the first saying because this [explanation] informs that all deeds are futile except those by which the Face of Allāh, the Exalted are sought, from the righteous deeds that conform with the legislation. As for the first saying then it necessitates that all essences are temporal and perishing, except the essence of the Exalted and Sublime. For He is the First and the Last who is before everything and after everything.
28:88.author: Ibn Kathīr (d.774H)

28:88.text: And do not invoke alongside Allāh another deity, rather, be sincere to Allāh in your worship because There is no deity [worthy of worship in truth] except Him. Hence, there is no one that deserves to be given devotion, and to be loved and worshipped except Allāh, the Perfect, the Everlasting, Everything except His Face will perish. So when everything besides Him will perish and disappear, then worshipping that which is perishing and futile is the most extreme of futility and corruption.
28:88.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

28:88.text: Editorial Note: The Face of Allāh is an attribute of His essence which follows the general principle of the absence of likeness (tamthīl) to His creation, similar to the rest of the attributes such as seeing, hearing, knowledge, will, power, life, mercy and so on. The phrase “Face of Allāh” (وَجْهُ الله) is used in the Qurʾān to refer to sincerity of action, that which is done to attain the pleasure of Allāh, to attain Paradise and the ultimate reward thereafter, which is to see the Face of Allāh. Refer to (6:52:), (76:9:) by way of example. Hence, in this verse in Sūrah al-Qasas, layers of meaning have been incorporated through the use of this wording, “Face of Allāh”. It indicates sincerity of action (ikhlāṣ) which is the essence of the word of Islām, the kalimah, to worship none but Allāh and to be sincere in that worship, seeking nothing but His pleasure. It also indicates that Allāh is Everlasting and Ever-Living who never dies, in contrast to His creation. It also indicates all actions done for the sake of others will be in vain and will perish. This cluster of meanings reinforces what came before in the verse: And do not invoke alongside Allāh another deity. There is no deity [worthy of worship in truth] except Him, and this is from the beauty of the Qurʾān in its subtle expressions, with layers of meaning having complete congruency, coherence and harmony. This verse prohibits invoking other deities which are created, temporal and perishing. It affirms the reality and truth of Tawḥīd, and then brings an expression, Everything except His Face will perish, with a cluster of meanings that reinforce what came before it—and in a manner that encourages and incites the reader to observe and abide by what has been commanded in the verse.Hence, there is the Tawḥid of al-Asmāʾ wal-Ṣifāt, of al-Rubūbiyyah and Ulūhiyyah in this verse as well as the prohibition of shirk.

33:56.text: It’s meaning is that Allāh showers His mercy upon the Prophet and praises him. And His saying ...and His Angels... means that the Angels invoke Allāh for mercy upon His Prophet. And the Exalted’s saying (يُصَلُّونَ), the concealed pronoun [in this verb] returns back to the noun ‘the Angels’ and not to ‘Allāh’ the Exalted because the mention of Allāh—the Mighty and Majestic—is singled out (separated) from the mention of others out of glorification. Muqātil said: ‘As for the ṣalāt of Allāh, it is forgiveness, as for the ṣalāt of the Angels, it is asking for forgiveness for him [the Prophet]’.
33:56.author: Imām al-Ṭabarānī (d. 360H)

33:56.text: Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: Ṣalāt from Allāh is mercy. And from the creatures—the angels, men and jinn—it is standing, bowing, prostration, supplication and glorification. And ṣalāt from the birds and beasts is glorification’.
33:56.author: Ibn Manẓūr (d. 711H)

33:56.text: Ṣalāt from Allāh is His mercy and pleasure. From the Angels it is supplication and asking for forgiveness. And from the ummah, it is supplication and veneration of His command.
33:56.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

33:56.text: Al-Bukhārī said: “Abū al-ʿĀliyah said: ‘The ṣalāt of Allāh the Exalted is His praise of [the Prophet] in the company of the Angels. The ṣalāt of the Angels is their supplication.’ And Ibn ʿAbbās said: ‘( يُصَلُّونَ ) means they invoke blessings [upon the Prophet]’. This is what al-Bukhārī related from them in muʿallaq form. And Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī also related this from Abū al-ʿĀliyah through al-Rabīʿ bin Anas. Its like has also been related from al-Rabīʿ... And Abū ʿĪsā al-Tirmidhī said: ‘Sufyān al-Thawrī and others from the people of knowledge said: The ṣalāt of the Lord is mercy. The ṣalāt of the Angels is seeking of forgiveness’.”
33:56.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774)

33:56.text: The intent behind this verse is that Allāh the Sublime and Exalted informed His servants of the status held by His Servant and Prophet [Muḥammad] with respect to Him in the Highest Company [of Angels] in that He praises [the Prophet] among the near Angels. And that the Angels themselves ask for forgiveness, mercy and blessings for him. Then He, the Exalted, commanded the inhabitants of the lower world to send ṣalāt (supplicate for blessings and mercy for him) and invoke salām upon him so that the praise of the two worlds, both the higher and the lower, are combined in him.
33:56.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

33:56.text: Citing Ibn al-Athīr: It is said that its origin (i.e. of the word ṣalāt) in the language is (تَعْظِيم), veneration. And the specified [daily] prayer (الصَّلَاة) is named ṣalāt due to what it comprises of the veneration of the Lord, the Blessed and Sublime... As for our saying: ‘O Allāh, send ṣalāt upon Muḥammad’, its meaning is: Make him great in the world by raising his mention, making his call uppermost, and his legislation to remain. And [make him great] in the hereafter by granting him intercession for his nation and multiplying his reward.
33:56.author: Ibn Manẓūr (d. 711H)

33:56.text: Editorial Note: Within the above is a refutation of those dishonest Christian evangelists who claim—upon complete and utter ignorance—that this verse is stating that Allāh worships the Prophet. The tactic employed by these evangelists—after they fail to validate their false doctrine of the divinity of the Prophet Jesus (عليه السلام) and of the trinity through their own distorted scripture—is to look for Islāmic texts which they can twist in order to make it appear that divinity or worship is being granted to other than Allāh. This verse is one such example. This then allows them to say: ‘Look, you too have associationism (shirk) in your religion.’ And this forms part of their evidence for the truth of their religion in which Jesus is deified and worshipped. This is from their ignorance as well as lack of honesty and clutching at straws.

And a party said: “In this speech is an omission [of the verb yuṣallī], and the meaning [of the sentence therefore] is, (إن الله يصلّي وملائكته يصلون) ‘Verily, Allāh sends blessings, mercy and the Angels send mercy, blessings [by invoking Allāh for them]’. There is no combined pronoun [in the verb yuṣallūna] in this verse therefore. ”
33:56.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

33:56.text: Refer also to (33:43:) in which Allāh confers praise, blessings and mercy (which are the meanings of ṣalāt) upon the believers and likewise (2:157:).

33:43.text: Ṣalāt from Allāh is His praise of the servant in the gathering of the Angels, it was related by al-Bukhārī from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, and it was also related by Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī from al-Rabīʿ bin Anas from him [Abū al-ʿĀliyah]. And other said that ṣalāt from Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, is mercy.
33:43.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

33:43.text: He, Exalted be His remembrance, says: Your Lord whose mention you make frequently and whom you glorify in the morning and evening, when you do that, then He is the one who shows mercy to you and praises you, and the Angels invoke Him for you. It is also said that the meaning of ( يُصَلِّـي عَلَـيْكُمْ وَمَلائِكَتُهُ ) means that He spreads beautiful mention of you among His servants.
33:43.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

33:43.text: His, the Exalted’s saying: ( هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُمْ ), Ibn ʿAbbās said: "When the verse Indeed, Allāh confers [His] grace and blessing upon the Prophet, and His angels [ask Him to do so]. was revealed, the Emigrants and Helpers said: ‘This is for you specifically O Messenger of Allāh, and there is nothing in it for us.' So Allāh the Exalted revealed this verse." I say: This bounty from Allāh the Exalted to this ummah is from the greatest of bounties.
33:43.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

33:43.text: His, the Exalted’s saying: ( هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكُم وَمَلآئِكَتُهُ ) has four sayings: First: It is His praise, said by Abū al-ʿĀliyah. Second: It is His generosity, kindness, said by Sufyān. Third: It is His mercy, said by al-Ḥasan. Fourth: It is His forgiveness, said by Ibn Jubayr. And regarding the ṣalāt of the Angels, there are two sayings: First: It is their supplication, said by Abū al-ʿĀliyah. Second: It is their seeking of forgiveness [for the believers], said by Muqātil bin Ḥayyān.
33:43.author: Al-Māwardī (d. 450H)

33:43.text: And ṣalāt from Allāh is mercy (raḥmah). ʿAdiyy bin al-Raqāʾ (a poet) said: ‘May Allāh shower mercy (ṣallā) upon a man to whom I have bid farewell and complete His favour upon him and increase it.’ And al-Rāʿī (a poet) said: ‘May al-Raḥmān (the Most-Merciful) shower mercy (ṣallā) upon Ghazzah and her daughter, Laylā. And may He shower mercy upon her other neighbours too.’ And as for the ṣalāt of Allāh upon His Messenger, it is His mercy towards him and making beautiful praise of him.
33:43.author: Ibn Manẓūr (d. 711H)

33:43.text: Editorial note: Christian evangelists—in their ignorance of the language of the Arabs—do not understand that the word ṣalāt (الصلاة) was applied to the prayer of the Muslims after Islām and after the revelation of the Qurʾān. The prayer consists of numerous affairs including: standing, bowing, prostrating, praising, extolling, invoking and others. So this word, ṣalāt extended the original linguistic meaning and idea to incorporate other aspects, to turn it into a technical term to refer to a ritual act of worship. The same is the case with zakāt (الزكاة), which literally means growth and purity, but technically, refers to the obligatory charity. Once this is clear, then these terms refer to a cluster of meanings. Upon this, the word can be used to refer to its original meaning alone, or a part of its original meaning, or a technical meaning which is either more specific or extensive. And hence, ṣalāt in relation to Allāh, means His praise, benevolence, generosity, blessing, bounty, mercy. And in relation to the Angels, it means their invocation for blessing and mercy upon the Prophet and for the Believers. And from the Believers it means the same, when they invoke blessings and mercy upon the Prophet. However, when taken with its technical meaning, then it means the ritual prayer performed by Muslims. Hence, we look in amazement at these Christians and both laugh and have pity for them at the same time, as they continue in their misguidance, trying to validate their polytheism and deification of Jesus (عليه السلام), a lofty Prophet of Allāh, and after failing to do so, trying to tell Muslims that they, as Christians,—after 1400 years—have discovered that Allāh prays and worships according to the Qurʾān—something that the Pagan Arabs who were the masters of the Arabic language failed to realise! But, these Christians in the 15th century hijrah have realised it! Then when they are refuted, they say: You are playing games with the Arabic language. We ask them to return back to their senses, display sincerity and not let arrogance and pride make them reject the truth. Abandon your polytheism and your Greco-Roman Pagan Christianity and return back to the Islām and Tawḥīd of Jesus (عليه السلام) and the Prophets before him.

Ṣalāt from Allāh is mercy. From the Angels it is seeking forgiveness for the Believers. And it is said: Ṣalāt from Allāh upon the servant is spreading beautiful remembrance of him among His servants. And it is said: Praising him. Editorial Note: Upon this, in (33:56:) Allāh’s ṣalāt upon His Prophet is mentioning him with praise among the highest company of Angels and also spreading beautiful praise and mention of His Propet among His servants. And this is something that is witnessed and known, for the Prophet has beautiful and recurring mention on the earth. Likewise, for His believing servants, His ṣālāt upon them is His mercy and praising them in the company of Angels, and also spreading good mention of them.
33:43.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

33:43.text: Refer also to (33:56:) which is related the revelation of this verse and likewise (2:157:).

35:27.text: He, the Exalted mentions His creation of contrasting [opposite] entities but whose foundation is one [and the same] and whose [source] material is one, and within which there is [such diversity and difference that is observed and known. [This], in order to indicate the perfection of His power and His amazing wisdom. From which is that Allāh the Exalted sends down water from the sky and produces therewith such diversity of fruits and variety of plants and vegetation that is observed by the onlookers. However, the water is but one water and the earth [soil] is but one soil. Also, the mountains which Allāh has made as [stabilising] pegs for the earth. You will find that they are intertwined [in their differing colours], rather, even a single mountain will have a variety of colours. It will have white tracts [or streaks], and likewise red and yellow tracts, and likewise, those which are intensely black.
35:27.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

37:96.text: Allāh the Sublime informed that He is their creator and the creator of the idols which they fashioned—and which only became idols through their deeds. Hence, that label does not fall upon them [the idols] except after their deeds [in fashioning them]. Since He, the Sublime, is the Creator, it necessitates the soundness of this unrestricted statement [of Allāh being the Creator of the both the material and the deeds performed to give the idols their shape and form]. I mean in terms of their substance and their form. For if their form is created by Allāh, just as their substance is created by Him, then it is binding that He is also the Creator of the very deeds through which their forms came to be, because such deeds arose through their motions.
37:96.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

37:96.text: This [verse] is a proof against the Muʿtazilites with respect to the actions of the servants [being created]. This is because Allāh—lofty be His majesty—did not create the idol in its carved, shaped form in the way that He created all other forms. And these people did not worship the material from which they carved out the idol in the [original, natural] form with which Allāh created it. So how can Ibrāhīm (صلى الله عليه وسلم) alongside his prophethood and close friendship [with Allāh] lie upon them and rebuke them for that which they did not do [if the claims of the Muʿtazilah are correct]? This is because these people did not worship stone or wood before carving and shaping them. He [Ibrāhīm] rebuked them for what they did, and their acts of worship fell upon the form of the carved idol and not upon the [original] thing from which it was carved out. As such, His saying and the deeds performed by you cannot be applied except to the carving [stated textually in the previous verse], which is an action, or upon [the carving] and likewise to other actions as well. And due to His saying being applied from these two [angles], it is a proof against them [the Muʿtazilah]. The Muʿtazilites claim that man is the creator of his own actions, outside the domain of Allāh’s will and power and as such, guidance and misguidance is not willed and decreed by Allāh. This verse is one of many refutations against them in the Qurʾān.
37:96.author: Al-Imām Muḥammad bin ʿAlī al-Qaṣṣāb (d. 360H)

37:96.text: There are two meanings in the verse. The first is: “Allāh created you and the actions you perform.” Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H) prefers this view and cites from Imām al-Bukhārī’s work “Khalq Afʿāl al-ʿIbād” who cites with his chain from Hudhayfah (رضي ا لله عنه) that he said: “Verily Allāh is the maker of every maker and his act of making.” The second is: “Allāh created you and the things you create.” And this is explained by Ibn al-Qayyim and others. Both meanings are contained in the verse, and hence it means: “Allāh created you, and hence the actions you perform, and hence, every item or product you create, make or manufacture is also created by Him.” Within this, there is also a proof against the atheists and materialists and this can be illustrated through the example of automated machines that are used in industry such as in the production of automobiles or 3D-printers that are able to create many types of products, including homes. The true creators of the end products and of the actions performed by these machines are the human creators of those machines, whose highly-developed technical and engineering knowledge, skill and wisdom is manifest through their craftsmanship. However, these machines have no free will and are unable to reflect. They are programmed to do what they do without reflection and choice. Humans have been given hearing, seeing, reflection, intelligence, choice and ability through which they choose, act and create. Their actions and what results from them are created by Allāh, though they are the performers of those actions through the choice and ability given to them. Hence, whilst He is the creator of all human deeds, humans are the performers of their own deeds, and will be held to account for them. Everything ever created and manufactured by humans is a creation of Allāh and every action performed by them is a creation of Allāh. As such—just as an automobile is proof of the existence, knowledge, wisdom, will and ability of the creator(s) of the automation procedures and machines—then likewise, every manufactured item is proof of its Creator, Allāh. Similarly, what is created by animals, such as a spider’s web, and a bird’s nest and so on, these prove His existence, knowledge, will, power and wisdom. Allāh is the creator of these things because he programmed and guided these creatures to these types of actions by which these things come to be. Thus, entities (the creatures), their actions and the end products of those actions are all evidence for His existence and His all-encompassing will and power. This overwhelming, compelling evidence for His rubūbiyyah (lordship) necessitates that He be singled out with gratitude and worship.

37:125.text: Baʿl is the name of an idol they used to worship, and it is why their city was called Baʿlabek. Mujāhid and ʿIkrimah said: “Baʿl means ‘lord (master)’ in the language of the people of Yemen.”
37:125.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

37:125.text: Muqātil said: It was an idol that Ilyās smashed and then he fled from them. Satan used to enter into Baʿl’s interior and speak with his misguided legislation, and its keepers would memorise and teach it to the people. They are the people of Baʿlabek in the lands of Shām, and their city was named after it.
37:125.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

39:4.text: Then, He, the Exalted, explained that He has no offspring, unlike the claims of the ignorant polytheists with respect to the Angels [that they are His daughters], or the obstinate among the Jews and Christians with respect to Ezrah (9:30:) and Jesus. So He, the Blessed and Exalted said: If Allāh wished to take a son (for Himself), He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills (as a son). Meaning, the affair would have been other than what they have claimed (of His having or taking a son or daughters for Himself). And this [i.e. wishing to take a son] is a condition whose occurrence is not necessitated nor permitted. Rather, it is impossible. He only intended to declare them ignorant in what they asserted and claimed, just as He, the Mighty and Majestic said: (21:17:), and also (43:81:). So this is from the angle of [stating] the condition, and it is permitted to attach a condition to what is impossible on account of the objective of the speaker (in doing so). And the Exalted’s saying But Sublime (is He from such a thing). He is Allāh, the One, the Subduer (who is never overcome). Meaning, Exalted, pure and sanctified is He from that He should have a son, for He is the One, the Uniquely One, the Self-Sufficient Master (who is free of needs) whilst everything else is a slave to Him, and needy of Him.
39:4.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

39:4.text: This is a corroboration of what has preceded of the invalidation of the saying of the polytheists that the Angels are daughters of Allāh. [This is due to what] it comprises of the absolute impossibility of Him, the Sublime, having a son. If He wished to take a son, then taking a son in reality, would be impossible, and that would never arise unless He chooses from what He creates whatever He wills (as a son). Meaning, chooses from the generality of His creation whatever He wills to choose, because there is nothing in existence besides Him except that it is His creation. And it is not correct for a creation to be a son of the Creator due to the absence of kinship and likeness between them. Hence, the only thing remaining is that He chooses a servant, as is afforded through the use of expression of al-Iṣtifāʾ (choosing) in place of taking (al-Ittikhādh). So the meaning of the verse is that if He wished to take a son, then something else would have taken place which is not ‘taking a son’ but rather, it would have been choosing one of His creatures (to be named as a son). For this reason, He the Sublime, exalted Himself from ‘taking a son’ in absolute terms, saying Sublime (is He from such a thing), meaning exalted is He from that.
39:4.author: Al-Shawkānī (d. 1250H)

48:29.text: Imām Mālik said: “In whoever’s heart there is agitation towards any of the Companions of Allāh’s Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم) then this verse falls upon him.”
48:29.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

49:6.text: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said: In this verse is evidence for the acceptance of the report of one person when he is trustworthy, because verification was commanded in the verse for conveying the report of a sinful, disobedient person. He whose disobedience is established, then by consensus, his reports are invalidated, because reporting is a trust, and disobedience is an indicator of the invalidation [of trust].

49:9.text: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H): Al-Bukhārī and others used this as evidence that [a person] does not exit from faith through sin, even if it is great, not as is said by the Khawārij and whoever followed them from the Muʿtazilah and their likes.

Imām al-Saʾdī (d. 1376H) said: Meaning, [Allāh loves] those who are just in their judgements bewteen the people, and [are just] in all positions that they hold, until this can even include the justice of a man towards his family and dependents, in fulfilling their rights. And in the authentic ḥadīth [related by Muslim]: “Those who are just, then with Allāh they are upon pulpits of light, those who are just in their judgements, [towards their] families, and in the positions they are given.

49:10.text: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H) said: This is a covenant that Allāh has placed between the believers, that when there is to be found from any person, whether in the eastern or western part of the world, belief in Allāh, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers and the Last Day, then he is a brother to the beievers with a brotherhood that necessitates that the believers love for him what they love for themselves and dislike for him what they dislike for themselves.

49:11.text: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said (abridged): This verse, according to Ibn ʿAbbās was revealed in relation to Thābit bin Qays who mocked a man for not making space for him to sit in the mosque, close to the Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم). According to al-Ḍahhāk, the verse was revealed in relation to Banū Tamīm who were mentioned earlier (49:4). The belittled the poor among the Companions after seeing their ragged condition. Mujāhid said: “It is the rich mocking the poor.” Ibn Zayd said: “Let not the one whose sin Allāh has concealed mock the one whose sin Allāh has exposed, for perhaps making his sin apparent in the world is better for him in the hereafter.” In summary, it is befitting that no one embark upon mocking the one he sees in a ragged condition, or who has some ailment in his body, or who is not skilled in conversation—for perhaps he is more sincere and of more pious a heart than the one who does not have his shortcomings—whereby he falls into oppressing himself by belittling the one whom Allāh has given respect.

Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said (abridged): Nor insult one another Al-Ṭabarī said: “(اللمز) Insulting occurs through the hand (by pointing), the eye, the tongue and through indication whereas (الهمز) only occurs with the tongue.” Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatādah and Saʿīd bin Jubayr said: “Do not revile each other.” Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: “Do not curse each other.” And it has been said: “From the happiness of a man is that he preoccupies himself with his own flaws away from the flaws of others.”

Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said: How evil is the label of disobedience after faith, meaning: How evil it is that a man be labelled disbeliever, or fornicator after his Islām and after his repentance, it was said by Ibn Zayd. And it is said that whoever gave his brother an insulting nickname or mocked him, is a sinner (fāsiq).

Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said (abridged): …nor call each other with (offensive) nicknames Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid said: A man would be blamed for his (prior) disbelief after his Islām, with the saying “O Jew” and “O Christian”, so this verse was revealed. Qatādah said: “It is the saying of a man to another, “O sinner”, “O hypocrite.”

49:12.text: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d 671H) said: It is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs [of al-Bukhārī and Muslim] from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: Beware of suspicion for suspicion [that is expressed] is the falsest of speech, and do not seek information (about others), nor spy (upon others), nor bid over one another (leading to price inflation), nor envy one another, nor hate one another, and nor turn your backs on each other [out of enmity]. But be servants of Allāh, brothers. The wording is al-Bukhārī’s. Our scholars have said: Suspicion here (in the ḥadīth) and in the verse is the conjectural suspicion (تهمة). That which is subject to caution and prohibition is the suspicion having no reason to justify it, such as the one who is suspected of a shameful deed or drinking an intoxicant for example, without anything manifesting from him which necessitates that. The evidence that the suspicion (الظن) here is with the meaning of (التهمة) is the Exalted’s saying ( وَلاَ تَجَسَّسُوا ) do not spy. This is because the conjectural suspicion may occur to him and then he desires to seek information on that, investigating it, watching, listening, in order to corroborate the suspicion which occurred to him. So the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) prohibited from that.

Imām al-Qurṭubī (d 671H) said: That which distinguishes suspicions which are to be avoided from others [that can be harboured] is that everything for which a valid sign (indication) or apparent reason is not known, it is unlawful and is obligatory to avoid. This is when the one against whom suspicion is held is one from whom prudence and rectitude are testified for, and trustworthiness is perceived from him outwardly. To have a corrupt suspicion about him and to betray [what is known about him] is unlawful. This differs from the one about whom it is known among the people that engages in the doubtful, and commits vile things in the open.

49:13.text: The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: Indeed, Allāh does not look at your appearances and possessions, but He look at your hearts and deeds. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Jāmīʿ (no. 1862). He (صلى الله عليه وسلم) also said: Honour is [itself] wealth, and nobility lies in fear [of Allāh]. Ṣaḥīḥ Ibn Mājah (no. 3418). He (صلى الله عليه وسلم) also said: There is no superiority for an Arab over a non-Arab, and nor a non-Arab over an Arab, and nor a white person over a black person and nor a black person over a white person, except through piety. Mankind is from Ādam, and Ādam is from dust. Ṣaḥīḥ, al-Albānī in Sharḥ al-Taḥāwiyyah.

Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H) said: The Exalted informs that He created the sons of Ādam from a single source, foundation and as a single species, all of them, male and female. All of them return back to Ādam and Eve. However, Allāh the Exalted spread forth from them many men and women and separated them into nations and tribes, meaning small and large [groups]. This is so that they can know each other, for if each of them kept to himself, [the objective] of knowing each other would not have been realised, from which there arises mutual support and aid, inheritance and performance of obligations towards relatives. However, Allāh made them nations and tribes so that these and other affairs can be realised, which rest upon acquaintance and meeting of genealogies. But honour (nobility) is through piety, so the most honourable of them in the sight of Allāh is the most pious of them, which is the most abundant of them in obedience and refraining from disobedience, not the one with most relatives and people, and nor the noblest of them in lineage. Allāh the Exalted is all-Knowing, all-Aware, He knows who among them abides by fear of Allāh, openly and inwardly from the one who does not abide by that, openly and inwardly. So he rewards everyone with what he deserves. And within this verse is evidence that knowing lineage is desired legislatively because Allāh made them nations and tribes for that purpose.

49:14.text: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H) said: These bedouins mentionend in the verse were not Hypocrites [outright] but they were Muslims in whose hearts faith had not settled firmly. So they claimed for themselves a station greater than the one they had reached, so they were disciplined for that.

Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H) said: What has been benefited from this noble verse is that faith (Īmān) is more specific than submission (Islām) as is the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jamāʿah. It is indicated [also] by the ḥadīth of Jibrīl (عليه الصلاة والسلام) when he asked about Islām, then about Īmān, then about Īḥsān. So he moved from the more general, to the specific, to the more specific.

49:15.text: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said: Meaning, [those] who believed and thereafter neve doubted and who corroborated that through jihād and righteous actions. It is they who are the truthful in their faith, not those who submitted for fear of deathh and hoping in acquisition [of goods]. When these verses were revealed, the bedouins swore that they are believes inwardly and outwardly, so then Allāh revealed… the verse that follows.

49:16.text: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H) says: He says: Allāh, whom you are informing that you are believers, is the Knower of all that is in the Seven Heavens and the Seven Earths, nothing whatsover is hidden from Him. So how can you inform him of [what is in your hearts] of religion and what you are upon of [alleged] faith, while nothing secret in Heaven or Earth is hidden from him.

Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H) said: This is inclusive of all things, from which are [the things held] in the hearts of belief and disbelief, righteousness and sinfulness. For He the Exalted knows all of that and gives recompense for it. If good, then with good and if evil, then with evil.

50:1.text: The Exalted swears by the Glorious Qurʾān, meaning that it is vast in meaning, multifaceted [in its approach], of abundant blessings, of plentiful goodness. Majd means vast and great in its descriptions. The most worthy of speech to be described with this is the Qurʾān—that which comprises the sciences [of divinity, the unseen, the hereafter and the likes] of the earlier and later [nations], that which comprises the most complete type of eloquence, and of words which are most laden with meaning. And the most comprehensive and beautiful of meanings. All of this necessitates perfection in following it, haste in complying with it and gratitude to Allāh for the favour [in revealing it to us].
50:1.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

50:1.text: Qāf is from the letters of the alphabet mentioned at the beginning of chapters such as Ṣād, Nūn, Alif Lām Mīm, Ḥā Mīm, Ṭā Sīn and others. It is narrated from some of the Salaf that they said Qāf is a mountain that surrounds the entire Earth and it is called the Mountain of Qāf. And it is as if this is—And Allāh knows best—from the fables of the Children of Israel which some people took from them on the basis of the permissibility of reporting affairs from them which are neither believed or rejected. In my view, this and its likes are from the fabrications of some of their heretics by which they deceive people about the affair of religion, similar to how in this [Islāmic] nation—alongside the lofty status of its scholars, memorisers and leaders—ḥadīths (traditions) have been fabricated against the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). [If this is the case with this nation] then how about the Children of Israel given the lengthy period of time, the scarcity of critical scholars [of memorisation and transmission] among them, their consumption of intoxicants, their distortion of words from their proper places and their alteration of the Book of Allāh and His Signs. The Legislator only permitted narrating from them in his saying, “Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm in it”, with respect to what reason allows. As for what is impossible in reason, is judged to be false, and it being a lie is overwhelming, then it is not of this type [that is permitted to narrate]. Ibn Kathīr goes on to say that many of the Salaf and the Khalaf (later ones) cited abundantly from the People of the Book in interpreting the Qurʾān, which they were not in need of doing. And this is one of the angles from which atheists and apostates criticise the Qurʾān today, due to what they find of such narrations being transmitted in the books of Qurʾān commentary.
50:1.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

50:17.text: This verse is connected to and follows from the previous verse, al-Qurṭubī explains: Meaning, that we are closer to him than his jugular vein when the two receivers, which are the two angels entrusted with him, receive [his deeds, which they record]. Meaning, that we are more knowledgeable of his various states and we do not need any angel to informs [us], but they (the two angels) are both entrusted with him in order to make the proof binding against him [on the Day of Judgement].
50:17.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

50:29.text: Al-Qurṭubī: “It is said that The word [of justice] that comes from Me will not be changed refers to (6:160:) and (50:29:).”

51:20.text: Within it are signs indicative of the greatness of its Creator and His splendid power. [From these signs] are what He has sown of various types of plants and and created of animals, and [what He has spread out of] lands and [fixed therein] of mountains, as well as the desert lands, rivers and oceans. [Likewise], the variation in the languages and colours of people, and their ability to desire alongside their faculties and powers [through which they act]. And likewise, what exists between them of variation in their intellects, cognitive abilities (in understanding), their movements, and their happiness and sadness. And [likewise] what exists in their bodily composition of wisdoms in that each and every one of their limbs has been placed in the exact place and position that they are in need of it to be in.
51:20.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

51:47.text: The claim of the contemporary people of kalām—the Muslim apologists who subject the interpretation of the Book to the conjectures of the disbelievers—that this verse is a proof for the Big Bang expansion, and the Qur’ān therefore preceded modern science, is a fabrication against the Book of Allāh and has no basis in truth. The iʿrāb (grammatical structure) of the verse indicates that the correct meaning of the verse is “We made the heaven to be vast whilst we were constructing it with power.” The particle waw in (وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ) is adverbial (ḥāliyyah) which means that in the course of constructing the heaven, Allāh the Exalted made it expansive and vast. These contemporary people of kalām are traversing the same path as the Jahmites of old who subjected the Book to speculative interpretations and interpolations in order to make it agree with the science and philosophy of the day.
We have made expansive its space (area), raising it without any pillars until it stands alone as it is.
51:47.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

51:47.text: We are possessors of great vastness (in ability) in creating it (the heaven) and creating what we wish to create and in (our) power over it... the powerful (is what is meant by the one who is mūsiʿ)... He, lofty be His majesty, made it expansive.
51:47.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

51:47.text: [And verily we made it expansive] in its area and space and we are also expansive upon our servants with sustenance.
51:47.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

51:47.text: Al-Mūsiʿ is the one possessing abundance and the meaning is we are possessors of vastness in our creation of it and other than it, we are not incapable of that. It is also said: We are able (qādirūn) with the meaning of ability (ṭāqah) and power (qudrah). It is also said: We are expansive in providing sustenance through rain.
51:47.author: Imām al-Shawkānī (d. 1250H)

51:47.text: Meaning, that we constructed it and the sentence is an adverbial one (jumlah ḥāliyyah), meaning that we made it whilst being expansive therein (in its making), similar to the saying, ‘Zayd come whilst he was rushing’ meaning he came rushing. Thus, [the heaven] is as though the earth and what covers it of water and air are like a dot in the middle of a [large] circle. And Ibn Zayd said something close to this which is that the expansiveness returns back to the heaven [in comparison to the earth]. It is also said, we are expansive in strength, power, meaning we are able from ability (wusʾ, ṭāqah). And al-Ḥasan said, ‘We expand the sustenance through rain and water’.
51:47.author: Abu Ḥayyān al-Andalūsī (d. 745H)

51:47.text: Ibn ʿAbbās said, ‘Powerful, able (قَادِرُون) and also from him, ‘Of vastness in providing sustenance to our creation.’ It is also said, ‘Possessors of vastness.’ And al-Ḍahhāk said, ‘Rich (أَغْنِيَاء), its evidence is the saying of Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, ...the wealthy (ٱلْمُوسِعِ) according to his ability... (2:236). Al-Ḥasan said, ‘Able, (مُطِيقُون)’.
51:47.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

51:49.text: [His saying] And of everything We created pairs [Meaning] two contrasting types and categories, such as: the heaven and the earth, the sun and the moon, the night and the day, the land and the sea, the level ground and the mountain, the winter and the summer, the jinn and men, the male and female, the light and the darkness, belief (īmān) and disbelief (kufr), happiness and misery, truth and falsehood, sweetness and bitterness. [His saying] that you may remember and take admonition, so that you know that the Creator of the pairs is singular, one (unpaired and unmatched). Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H) Maʿālim al-Tanzīl (1409H, Riyāḍ: Dār Ṭayyibah) 7/379. Added by: abuiyaad on 07-Jul-18
51:49.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

51:49.text: Meaning, all created things are in pairs: heaven and earth, night and day, sun and moon, land and sea, light and darkness, faith and disbelief, death and life, misery and happiness, paradise and hellfire. Until even the animals and plants. For this reason, He the Exalted said, that you may remember and take admonition, meaning, so that you may know that the Creator is one without any partner.
51:49.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

51:49.text: The opposite of (fard), single, solitary, one. It is said: Pair (zawj) or single (fard)... The Arabs apply (zawjayn) to two differing types, such as black and white and sweet and sour... And al-Ḥasan used to say regarding the Mighty and Majestic’s statement And of everything We created pairs , “The sky is one of a pair, the earth is one of a pair, the winter is one of a pair, the summer is one of a pair, the night is one of a pair, the day is one of a pair.”
51:49.author: Ibn Manẓūr (d. 711H)

53:32.text: From Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ( إِلاَّ ٱللَّمَمَ ) save the lesser sins: “Everything that is between the two limits. The prescribed limit in the world and the limit in the hereafter, then the prayer expiates for it and it is ‘the lesser sin’... As for the limit of the world, then it is every sin for which Allāh has obligated a punishment in the world. And as for the limit of the hereafter, then it is every deed whose performance Allāh has sealed with the Hellfire [as mentioned in what He revealed] and the punishment for which has been delayed for the Hereafter.
53:32.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

53:32.text: And the meaning of the verse ( إِلاَّ ٱللَّمَمَ ) save the lesser sins is: Except when he commits a fāḥishah (sin involving desire) once and then repents, and when it occurs and then ends (not returning to it again). This is the saying of Abū Hurayrah, Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan, and it is also the report of ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās... and some of them said: They are minor sins such as the glance, the winking of the eye (to solicit an encounter), the kiss and whatever is less than actual fornication. This is the saying of Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Hurayrah, Masrūq, al-Shaʿbī, and it is the report of Ṭāwūs from Ibn ʿAbbās.
53:32.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

53:32.text: (They are) those who avoid major sins and immoral deeds. Meaning, those who do what Allāh has commanded them of the obligations, the leaving of which is from the major sins. And who abandon the major prohibitions such as fornication, drinking intoxicants, consuming interest, murder and what is similar to that of the mighty sins. ( إِلاَّ ٱللَّمَمَ ) save the lesser sins, and these are the minor sins upon which a person does not persist. Or those which a servant falls into rarely, every now and then. So falling into these [types of sins] does not remove a person from being among the righteous (al-muḥsinīn). For this, alongside fulfilment of the obligations and abandonment of the prohibitions, enters (a person) under the forgiveness of Allāh which encompasses every single thing. Hence, He said: Indeed, your Lord is of vast forgiveness . Had it not been for His forgiveness, the servants and the lands would have perished. And had it not been for His forbearance the heaven would have fallen upon the earth and not a single creature would have been left upon its surface. For this reason, the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: ‘The five prayers, the jumuʿah to the next jumuʿah, and one Ramaḍān to the next Ramaḍān are an expiation for what is (done) in between them (of sins), so long as the major sins are avoided.’
53:32.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

53:45.text: That He originated the creation of the two mates [complimentary partners], the male and the female, and made them into spouses [for each other]. This is because the male is the spouse for the female and the female is the spouse for him. Thus, they are two spouses, each of them is a complimentary partner for the other.
53:45.author: Imām al-Tabari (d. 310H)

53:45.text: He explained the two spouses with His statement the male and the female, and this is the name of a category which comprises all living things, both those capable of speech [upon rational thought] and those unable to do so [such as the cattle]. Thus, He is alone in creating them.
53:45.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

53:45.text: What is intended by the two spouses is the male and female from every living thing.
53:45.author: Imām al-Shawkānī (d. 1250H)

53:44.text: Meaning: He caused death in this life and gave life in the hereafter. And it is said: He caused the fathers to die and gave life to the sons. And it is said: He caused the disbeliever to die [by making him unknown] and gave live to the believer [by making him known].
53:44.author: Al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

53:46.text: Imām al-Shanqīṭī (d. 1393H) said in Aḍwāʾ al-Bayān: And some of the scholars have said (مِن نُّطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَىٰ), meaning it is pre-determined by design to work in that way (tuqaddar) in that Allāh has decreed that pregnancy should be initiated through [the sperm]. Regarding the word (منى), in Lisān al-ʿArab of Ibn Manẓūr (d. 711H) there occurs: It is measurement, quantification, determination (القَدَر)... and it is said, (منى الله لك ما يسرك), meaning, may Allāh determine and decree for you what will please you. (p. 4283). Editorial note: This indicates two meanings in the verse as alluded by Imām al-Shanqīṭī based upon the meaning of (منى): a) that males and females are created through the emission of sperm [by the male] and b) that the sperm has been subject to prior determination and programming to lead to pregnancy and human development.
53:46.author: Imām al-Shanqīṭī (d. 1393H)

53:46.text: And this is from the greatest of evidences for the perfection in His power and His uniqueness in His tremendous might [of creative power] in that He created those living things, both the small and the large, from lowly (weak) sperm contained in despicable fluid. Then He caused it to grow and to reach perfection until it reaches what it reaches (of its final, mature form).
53:46.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

53:46.text: (مِن نُّطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَىٰ), estimated, determined, it was said by Abū ʿUbaydah. It is said (مَنَيت الشيء) when you pre-estimate and determine it, and (مُنِي له), meaning, it was estimated and determined for him. The poet said: (حَتّـى تُـلاَقِيَ مـا يَمْنِـي لَكَ الْمَانِـي), meaning, what the able and powerful is able to determine for you. Editorial Note: An exemplification of the meaning of qadar, taqdīr is given by Muslim scholars through the example of a tailor. In making a garment, he has to measure and determine the material before it is cut and sown. So the meaning here is one of “estimation, determination, calculation, measurement”.
53:46.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

54:14.text: Al-Baghawi (d. 516H) said: With our watch, and Muqātil bin Ḥayyān said: ‘With our protection.’ And Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H) said: With our watch and under our guard and protection. . This verse, along with other texts from the Book and Sunnah, affirms the attribute of Eyes for Allāh, and the principle in this respect, as it is with all the attributes of Allāh, is that they are affirmed with negation of any likeness to the creation. His attributes are unlike those of the creation, since His essence is unlike their essences, just in the same way that the attributes of the Jinn—who hear, see and speak—are unlike our attributes beause their essences are unlike ours.
