So when dissimilarity is comprehensible between two created things then the difference (in the reality of the essence and its attributes) between the Creator and created is even greater Thus, there is absolutely no caution in affirming the attributes Allāh has affirmed for Himself, and those who negate these attributes by claiming iet is anthromorphism (tashbīh, tajsīm), then they are misguided and in opposition to the Qurʾān, Sunnah and the way of the Salaf. It is tashbīh if it is said:”His hearing is like my hearing, His seeing is like my seeing, His hand is like my hand, His face is like my face” and so on, but it is not tashbīh if it is said: “He has hearing, seeing and a Hand and Face, but they are unlike our hearing, seeing, hands and face, because His essence is unlike ours and is uncreated”, and this is what the Salaf were upon.

54:24.text: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H) said: “This speech is from their misguidance and wretchedness for they showed arrogance towards following a messenger among men [calling them to worship Allāh alone] but did not reject that they should be worshippers of tree, stones and pictures.”

54:43.text: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H) said: If they [the Pagan Arabs] are better than them, it is possible for them to be saved from punishment, and they will not be afflicted with what afflicted with those evil ones. But the affair is not like that, for if they are not more evil than them, then they are not better than them [either].

54:47.text: The Exalted informs that the criminals are in misguidance, away from the truth, and in confusion, madness due to their doubts and confused opinions. This includes everyone who is described with this, of the disbeliever and innovator from all the [various] sects.
54:47.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

54:47.text: The Pagans disputed about Qadar, using it to validate and justify their polytheism. And in this ummah, the Qadariyyah negated Qadar on account of rationalities and made themselves the creators of their own actions outside the domain of Allāh’s knowledge (the earlier ones) and outside the domain of His will and creative power (the Muʿtazilah). Likewise, the Jabariyyah, following al-Jahm bin Ṣafwān, they claimed man is compelled in his action. All of these are disputants in the matter of al-Qadar.

55:1.text: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said: Saʿīd bin Jubayr and ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī said: ( الرَّحْمنُ ) The Most-Merciful, the opening of three chapters, when combined they become a name from the names of Allāh the Exalted: ( ن) ( حم) (الر). So all of these combined become ( الرَّحْمنُ ). Added by: abuiyaad on 30-Oct-23

55:33.text: The people of interpretation differed about His saying if you are able to pass beyond. Some of them said its meaning is that if you are able to pass the boundary regions of the heavens and earth such that you render your Lord incapable of reaching you, then do so. For you will never be able to do so except with authority from your Lord. They said that this statement will be said to them on the Day of Judgement... And others said that its meaning is that if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and earth [in order to flee death], then pass beyond them to flee death, but death will certainly reach you, and fleeing from it will not help you. Al-Ḍahhāk said: ‘No one will protect them from death and they will die and not be able to flee from it, there is no escape, even if they passed beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, they will remain under the authority of Allāh, and Allāh will take them by death.’
55:33.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

55:33.text: Meaning, when Allāh gathers them on the Day of Judgement, He will inform them of their incapacity and weakness and the perfection of His authority and the execution of His will and power. So He will say—informing them of their incapacity— O company of Jinn and Mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the boundary regions of the heavens and the earth , meaning, [if you are able] to find some actionable way to escape from the dominion and authority of Allāh Then pass [if you can]! You will never pass [them] except with power, authority [from Allāh]. Meaning, you will not escape from it except through strength and authority of your own, alongside perfect power. But how will they have that, whilst they are not even able to control benefit or harm for themselves, and nor death, life or resurrection?! Hence, in that place, no one will speak except with His permission. Nothing will be heard but whispering, and in that place [on that Day], the kings and the subjects, the leaders and those led by them, and the rich and poor will all be equal.
55:33.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

55:33.text: O company of Jinn and Mankind, if you are able to pass beyond, meaning, pass through and exit the boundary regions of the heavens and the earth, meaning, from their sides and outer limits then pass [if you can]!. Its meaning is that if you are able to flee from death by escaping from the boundary regions of the heavens and earth, then flee and escape from them. And the meaning is that wherever you are, death will reach yo, just as He, lofty be His mention, said: Wherever you may be, death will reach you (4:78:). And it is said: It will be said to them on the Day of Judgement, ‘If you are able to pass through the boundary regions of the heavens and earth and thereby render your Lord incapable of reaching you, then pass through [if you can]’, then pass [if you can]! You will never pass through except..., meaning, with authority. And it is said, with proof. And ṣulṭān is complete power, authority over an affair. So authority, power, proof, all of it is ṣulṭān. He intends that wherever you turn towards, you remain under my authority and power.
55:33.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

55:33.text: Meaning: You will not be able to flee from the command and decree of Allāh. Rather, He completely surrounds you and you are not able to remove yourself from His judgement, and nor from the execution of His command with respect to you. Wherever your go, you will be surrounded. And this is on the gathering plain [of the Day of Resurrection]. The Angels will encircle all of the creatures, in seven rows from every side and no one will be able to depart except with authority, meaning with the command of Allāh.
55:33.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

55:33.text: Editorial Note: From (55:31:) and (55:35:), the Qurʾān commentators state that the context of this verse is the Day of Judgement. The heavens and earth will have been altered and transformed (14:48:), and the people will be gathered, after resurrection, on the plain of the transformed earth. It is here where it will be said O company of Jinn and Mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the boundary regions of the heavens and the earth, with the meaning that if you are able to escape, then try to do so, but you will never be able to do so, except with authority and power from Allāh. This being an indication to their complete powerlessness on that day and being encompassed. As for the verse being a proof for “space travel”, then Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz bin Bāz (رحمه الله) stated: “As for His saying, the Sublime, in Sūrah al-Raḥmān... then it is not clear evidence for the possibility of ascending to the celestial bodies because the apparent meaning of the verse, from what is before (55:31:) and after it (55:35:), shows that Allāh the Sublime desired to explain the powerlessness of the two parties [of Jinn and Men] from being able to pass through the boundaries of the heavens and earth. Imām Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī (رحمه الله) and others from the scholars of tafsīr have mentioned numerous sayings in explanation of the verse, the best of them are two: The first, that the intent of the verse is the Day of Judgement. That Allāh has explained [in this verse] the inability of [Jinn and Men] to flee from its terrors. Ibn Jarīr gave preference to this view, and mentioned [as evidence] for what led him to choose this view the verse that comes after it (55:35:). The second saying is that the intent behind it is to explain the inability [of the Jinn and Men] to flee from death, because they have no power allowing them to flee from death. And upon these two sayings, the meaning of sulṭān is strength, power (quwwah). And from what we have mentioned, it is clear that there is no proof in this verse for the one who said that it indicates the possibility of ascending to the celestial bodies, and that “knowledge” is meant by the word sulṭān. It also becomes clear that the closest of sayings is that of the one who said that the Day of Judgement is intended by it... As for this world, then no one is able to pass through the boundaries of the constructed heavens, because they are protected by way of their guards and doors, whose mention has already preceded, and Allāh, the Sublime and Exalted, knows best.” Majmūʿ Fatāwā wa Maqālāt (1/254).

56:79.text: That which is correct regarding this verse is that the scrolls [which are] in the hands of the Angels are intended by it, due to numerous angles [of evidence]. From them is that He described it as maknūn (see 56:78) and that which is maknūn is whatever is concealed from the eyes. And this can only be in the scrolls that are in the hands of the Angels. And from them is that He said Which none can touch except the purified (muṭahharūn) and they are the Angels. If He intended the believers who purify themselves through ablution, He would have said, "Which none can touch except the (mutaṭahhirūn)".
56:79.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

57:8.text: There are two reasons for belief: The first is the call of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). The second is the covenant which Allāh took from us, and that is through what He (عز وجل) gave us of original disposition (fiṭrah), reason (ʿaql) and comprehension (fahm), by which we comprehend what benefits and harms us, and this is what is correct regarding the meaning of “covenant (mīthāq)”.
57:8.author: Shaykh Ibn al-ʿUthaymīn (d. 1421H)

57:20.text: Here, some of the affairs of life have been mentioned which are prevalent in people and which are not free from the wastage of noble aims, or incurring reprehensible evils. And these [affairs] are the foundations of the conditions of society in life. They are also foundations of the stages of individuals in their development [through life]. Play is the stage of infancy, amusement is the stage of adolescence, beautification is the stage of youth, boasting is the stage of middle-age and gathering [wealth] is the stage of old age.
57:20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr (d. 1393H)

58:2.text: The Qurʾān commentators and linguists have said that “ḍhihār” was pre-Islāmic divorce which represented an emphatic, permanent prohibition. I believe that it was a form of divorce among the people of Yathrib and its surrounding areas, due to their frequent mixing with the Jews. I do not believe it was known among the Arabs of Mecca, Tihamah, Najd and others, I have not come across that in their speech. What is apparent is that prior to Islām they used to mingle with the Jews and adopt their customs. The Jews would forbid a man from approaching his wife (for intercourse) from behind, and hence the word “back” (ḍhahr) appears in the formulation to exaggerate the prohibition, which is to say his wife is like his mother [in prohibition in marriage]. Hence, it is a hideous and terrible formulation [to use for the purpose of divorce].
58:2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr (d. 1393H)

59:2.text: Those intended are Banū al-Naḍīr, a tribe of the Jews, who settled the lands of Arabia, along with Banū Qurayḍhah, and the Jews of Khaybar, and all of them are from the offspring of Aaron (عليه السلام). They used to be called the “Cohenites” because they are from Aaron’s offspring, and he was the Israelite “Cohen”, which means the preserver of religious affairs by hand. The reason for their settlement in the lands of the Arabs was that Moses (عليه السلام) sent a faction of their ancestors to fight the Amalekites in the neighbouring Levant (Shām), but they failed to do so, and then Moses died shortly after that. When they learned about Moses’ death, they returned to the Israelites who said to them: “You disobeyed Moses, so do not enter our land.” So they left for the Arabian peninsula and [through the passing of generations] established townships for themselves around Yathrib (Madīnah). They became agriculturists and traders and had built numerous strong fortresses. Among them were people of affluence such as Samuel bin Adiya, Kaʿb bin al-Ashraf, Ibn Abī al-Ḥuqayq. From the core of those Jews were Banū al-Naḍīr, Banū Qurayḍhah and Khaybar. They were described as those who disbelieve because they disbelieved in the messengership of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) [despite their full knowledge that is the prophet that they were expecting based on the descriptions in their books]. And they were described as the People of Scripture, so that it is not thought that those intended are the Pagans of Mecca or the Pagans in Madīnah. The detail of the story is what is mentioned by the majority of the commentators that when the Muslims migrated to Madīnah, they, Banū al-Naḍīr, came to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and made a covenant of peace with him, which stated that they would remain neutral [between him and the Pagans]. This was after the Battle of Badr, when the Muslims defeated the Pagans of Mecca, and they [the Jews of Banū al-Naḍīr] did not expect the Pagans to be defeated. But when the Muslims were later defeated after the Battle of Uḥud, they broke their covenant with the Prophet and made a covenant with the Pagans [allying with them]. As it was the custom of the Jews to ally with the strong and powerful, the leader of Banū al-Naḍīr, Kaʿb bin al-Ashraf, went with forty riders and formed an alliance with the Pagans to help them fight the Muslims. When this [treachery and conspiracy] was revealed by Allāh to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), he sent Muḥammad bin Maslamah to kill Kaʿb bin al-Ashraf in his own fortress, and he did so. Further, in another affair, regarding assistance of payment of blood money for two men of the tribe of Banū ʿĀmīr—with which the Jews of Banū al-Naḍīr had an alliance—who had been killed by ʿAmr bin Umayyah al-Ḍamrī, the Jews of Banū al-Naḍīr conspired to treacherously kill the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) when he was going to meet them regarding the affair. But Allāh revealed their intentions to him. So the Muslims went to them in the month of Rabīʿ al-Awwal in 4 AH, and the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) ordered them to leave their homes and go into exile [as punishment for their treachery]. However, they refused and made war cries. ʿAbd Allāh bin Ubayy bin Salūl (a chief hypocrite) found his way to them and told them not to leave, and that if the Muslims fight them, they would support them, and if they are expelled, they would go with them, and that he had 2000 people on his side, along with [the Jews of] Qurayḍhah and their allies from the Arabs, such as Ghaṭfān. So the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) besieged them and Banū al-Naḍīr waited for ʿAbd Allāh bin Ubayy, Qurayḍhah and Ghaṭfān to come to their aid in repelling the Muslim army. But when they did not come to their aid, Allāh placed terror into their hearts. They then requested a truce with the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), but he refused and insisted that they leave and go into exile. So they made a condition that they be allowed to carry camel loads of their belongings. They began to destroy their own homes to take whatever they could use of wood and doors, and then left. Some of them went to the Levant (Shām), some of them went to Khaybar, some to the cities of Jericho and Adhraʿāt and a few went to al-Ḥīrah.
59:2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr (d. 1393H)

59:14.text: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H) said: They will not fight you, meaning the Jews all together except in fortified cities, meaning, they do not come out openly to fight you directly [man to man], but they fight you while fortifying themselves with cities and walls. Their enmity between themselves (the Jews and the Hypocrites) is severe, meaning, some of them are harsh towards others and their enmity to each other is severe. And it is said: Their enmity between themselves behind the walls and cities is severe, so when they come out to you (to fight), they are the most cowardly of Allāh’s creation. You think they are together, but their hearts are divided, split, at variance. Qatādah said: “The people of falsehood are at variance in their desires, at variance in their testimony, at variance in their actions, but they are united in showing enmity towards the People of Truth.” Mujāhid said: “He intends that the religion of the Hypocrites differs from the religion of the Jews.”

60:8.text: When the noble verses [that precede this one] were revealed—those which incited enmity towards the disbelievers [who oppressed, expelled and waged war against Muslims]—the believers thought that they applied to every situation, and so they adhered to them in a most complete way. As a result, they withheld from maintaining relations with their polytheist relatives and thought that this also entered into what Allāh had prohibited [in those verses]. So Allāh informed them that [such behaviour] does not enter into the unlawful, so He said Allāh does not forbid you—with respect to those who do not fight you because of religion and who do not expel you from your homes—from being kind towards them and behaving justly with them. Indeed, Allāh loves those who act justly. Meaning, Allāh does not prohibit you from kindness, maintaining relations, mutual goodness and justice with the polytheists, those from your relatives and others, so long as they did not undertake to fight you because of religion and to expel you from your homes. In such a case, there is nothing to prevent you from maintaining ties with them, there being no caution or corruption in maintaining ties with them in this situation. This is similar to what Allāh, the Exalted said regarding polytheist parents whose son is a Muslim: But if they both strive to make you associate others with Me [in worship]—a matter of which you have no knowledge—then do not obey them, but accompany them in the life of this world with kindness (31:15).
60:8.author: Imām al-Saʾdī (d. 1376H)

60:8.text: After discussing the various views regarding this verse, al-Ṭabarī says: The most correct of these statements is of the one who said that [this verse] pertains to all of the factions from the varying beliefs and religions. That you behave kindly towards them, and that you are just regarding them, because Allāh generalised with His saying, those who do not fight you because of religion and who do not expel you from your homes. So this applies to everyone who is characterised by this. He did not specify some as opposed to others in this regard.
60:8.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

60:8.text: Editorial Note: This is a decisive (muḥkam) verse and has not been abrogated and is a refutation of Islām haters, apostates, atheists and others characterised by ignorance, desires or both. The famous Qurʾān commentator Imām al-Shanqīṭī (d. 1393H) discussed this issue at length and brought numerous clear historical and textual evidences to establish that this verse has not been abrogated. He said: This (view) that has been deemed correct by Ibn Jarir (al-Ṭabarī) and which was authenticated by al-Shafiʿī (رحمه الله) is that which is necessitated by spirit of the Islamic legislation. He also used as evidence the verse in the Qurʾān which enjoins kindess and good treatment of polytheist parents, despite their efforts to draw their son or daughter into their polytheism (31:15:). In sealing his arguments, he stated: And we have lengthened the speech regarding this matter due to its importance and the dire need for it today. Refer to Aḍwā al-Bayān (6/1466 onwards).

The jurist Aḥmad bin Idrīs al-Miṣrī al-Qarāfī (d. 684H) explained the meaning of being kind towards them with the following words: To show gentleness to their weak, to satisfy the needs of their poor, to feed their hungry, to clothe their naked, to use gentle, kind speech to them from the angle of compassion and mercy towards them—not out of fear or inferiority—to bear whatever harm arises from them when they are our neighbours despite having the ability to end (their harm), doing this out of compassion for them, not out of fear or veneration of them. To supplicate for guidance for them, that they be made people of happiness, to advise them in all their affairs that pertain to their religion and [likewise] their worldly affairs. To protect them in their absence when anyone embarks upon harming them, to protect their wealth, their families, their honour and all of their rights and beneficial interests. That they are supported in repelling any oppression against them and delivering all their rights to them. A (Muslim) does all such acts of goodness towards them that one who is in a privileged position can possibly do towards the one who is under-privileged and likewise, [all acts of goodness] that [even] an enemy could possibly do towards an enemy, for all of that is from nobility in character and manners. It is desireable that all of what we do with respect to them is from this angle, not from the angle of pride and loftiness on our behalf and nor from the angle of belittling ourselves and exalting them through such actions towards them. Kitāb al-Furūq (3/14).

61:6.text: In Tārīkh Dimashq of the historian Ibn ʿAsākir (d. 1176 CE), it is related from Kaʿb al-Aḥbār—[a learned Jewish Rabbi who accepted Islām in the era of the Prophet]—through a number of chains that he said: I find in the Torah: He is my servant, Aḥmad, the chosen one. He is neither coarse nor rude in speech, and nor does he shout in the markets. He does not return evil with evil but he pardons and forgives. His birth is in Bakkā and his emigration is to Ṭābā and his dominion will be held in Shām (Syria). His nation are the ḥammādūn, they praise Allāh in every state and they glorify him in every abode. They wash their extremes [feet and hands], and cover their middle parts. They are the shepherds of sun [i.e. desert]. Their standing in rows in prayer and in fighting are the same. They are ascetics by night, lions by day. They have a reverberating sound like the sound of bees [when in prayer]. They pray whenever its time reaches them. Refer to Tārīkh Dimashq (1/183-189) under the chapter, “What has come regarding Shām being the seat of power of the people of Islām”.

The passage being referred to by Kaʿb is in the book of Isaiah (see 42:1) in which the name Aḥmad was explicitly mentioned. However, it was changed from Aḥmad (אהמד), which means “one that is beloved”, to Atmak (אתמך) which means “one that is upheld, supported” This alteration was either by copying error or by deliberate distortion. In the gospel named “Matthew” the same passage in Isaiah is quoted (see 12:18), and the author of that gospel was translating from the original semitic language into Greek or using the Septuagint translation (from Hebrew into Greek) . The Greek translation provides evidence that the original was “Aḥmad” because it was rendered as “agapaytos” in Greek which means “beloved”. This is the same as the meaning of Aḥmad (אהמד) in Hebrew. This becomes apparent by comparing Isaiah 42:1 in which the alteration has taken place (and which says, “whom I uphold”) with Matthew 12:18 (which says, “my beloved” or “the one I love”).

Isaiah 42:1 Behold my servant, whom I uphold (atmak); mine elect, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgement to the Gentiles. He will not cry out or raise His voice, nor make His voice heard in the streets. Matthew 12:18 Behold, my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved (Greek: agapaytos, Hebrew: Aḥmad) with whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice to the Gentiles. He will not quarrel or cry out; no one will hear His voice in the streets.

The Prophet whose coming is foretold by Isaiah is Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) who is from the descendants of Qedār, the son of Ishmāʿīl. The evidences from chapter 42 of the Book Isaiah are as follows: — Three titles of the Prophet are used: ʿabd (servant), aḥmad (“praised” in Arabic and “beloved” in Hebrew) and mukhtār (chosen one). — His lineage is mentioned as coming from Qedār, who is the second son of Ishmāʿīl, and they were residents of Fārān which is the Hijāz where Makkah and Madīnah are located. — He is sent to the goyīm, the non-Israelite heathens who are also described as those who fashion idols. Hence, this cannot be any prophet from the Israelites, Jesus included. — The mention of the “wilderness” is a reference to the desert and can be connected to the “wilderness of Paran” as mentioned in other places in the Bible and also to “Mount Paran” which is a reference to Mecca. — The mention of Selaʾ is a reference to the mountain with the same name which is just one mile away from the Prophet’s Mosque in Madīnah. The Muslims rejoiced when the Prophet came to Madīnah from Mecca. — Along with the mention of Qedār, the references to the Hijāz (Mecca and Madīnah) leave no doubt that this is an Arabian prophet known as Aḥmad (the praised) who will appear among the Arab idol-worshippers. — The “Spirit” (a reference to Gabriel) will be put on him (a reference to the sending of revelation). Refer to (16:102:), (26:193:) and the two verses after it. — A “new song” will be sung (the Qurʾān) and he will come with a fiery law (the Sharīʿah). — He will be victorious over the idol worshippers. — He will bring guidance and justice to the nations. — This Prophet, Servant of God and Chosen One is also referred to as (מְשֻׁלָּם) “meshullam” in the Hebrew, which means “he that is at peace” (which is Muslim) as occurs in Isaiah 42:19. This Prophet is one who “submits” to God. All of these are clear evidences of the Prophethood of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) which the Jews of Arabia knew full well, just as they knew their own sons (2:146:). So their rejection was upon knowledge, conceit and arrogance.

62:1.text: Since the days resemble each other and cannot be distinguished from each other by any attribute, whether inherent to the day itself or abstract in nature, then their differentiation was left only to numerical means. Hence, they made the names of the week to be derived from numbers, such as the second, the third, the fourth [and so on] or by way of events such as the day of Buʿāth (the place near Madīnah of the last encounter between the Aws and the Khazraj tribes prior to Islām) or the day of (the battle of) Badr or the day of Faṭḥ (victory), and from them is the day of Jumuʿah. There are two views regarding this. The first is due to the people gathering on this day for prayer. The second—and which is the correct view—is that it is the day in which the creation was brought together and perfected [through the creation of Ādam] and it is the day on which Allāh will gather together the first and later ones in order to make judgement.
62:1.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

62:1.text: Meaning, He is the Master, Owner of the Heavens and Earth who governs them with His rule and judgement and he is the Perfectly Pure, which means the one sanctified of all deficiencies, shortcomings, described with attributes of perfection. [His saying]: the All-Mighty, the All-Wise, its explanation has preceded more than once.
62:1.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

65:4.text: This verse relates to divorce and addresses numerous types of women in a divorce situation. They include: a) Women who have reached or passed menopause, b) the women who have never menstruated at all (due to inability to do so from a condition known as primary amenorrhea) and c) girls who have been married off by their fathers on grounds of beneficial interest. Regarding this third situation, it is when a father marries off his daughter whilst she is a minor—below the age of mental and physical maturity—due to some beneficial interest that would otherwise be lost. This situation can be found frequently in the history of nations all across the world and many examples exist among European royalty. Kings and queens married off their daughters at very young ages because a particular person of royalty, of good standing and character, well-to-do and of means was available. If they delayed marrying off their daughter, they would lose this potential husband to someone else’s daughter. Muslims jurists point out that a girl should not be married off until she has reached bulūgh (maturity) and has expressly given her permission, unless a clear beneficial interest in her getting married prior to this would be otherwise lost. Some Muslim jurists such as Shaykh Ibn al-ʿUthaymīn—who give primacy to the condition of permission—state that even if the father marries off his daughter due to a clear beneficial interest, his daughter should be given a choice if she wishes to continue with the marriage when she reaches maturity and is able to give or deny permission. Hence, the marriage would only be consummated if she has given her permission and when the father has allowed cohabitation. After the marriage contract, the time of cohabitation would then be decided by the parents. Keeping in mind that menstruation may not take place until the age of fifteen years or even later, it is possible for the husband and wife to engage in sexual relations prior to her menstruation if her guardian has allowed cohabitation. If the husband decides to divorce his wife, then this is the situation in which this ruling comes to play. A waiting of period of three months is to verify that she has not become pregnant, such that when the divorce is complete, she is free to remarry without there being any possibility of confusion about the real father of any child she bears. As for commencement of sexual relations, then Muslim jurists state the conditions of physical readiness and absence of any harm. The famous Muslim jurist, Imām al-Nawawī, said: “Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfah said that it is the ability to engage in intercourse that defines the time when a father allows his daughter to cohabit with her husband. This varies from one person to another and does not have a specific age, and this is what is correct.” Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (9/206). Thus, a father will decide when his daughter is ready to engage in sexual relations and allow cohabitation. The Muslim jurists also make clear that a marriage contract on its own does not allow sexual relations, but rather it is the principle based on the Prophetic tradition, There is no causing of harm or reciprocating harm. Hence, when there is physical readiness and absence of harm, then sexual relations can take place. And this would be evaluated and decided by the parents. Likewise, the Muslim jurists make clear that all harm in sexual activity must be absent before cohabitation is allowed, with the Shāfiʿite jurists holding that even if the husband requests cohabitation with the reassurance that he will not engage in sexual activity, the parents are not to release their daughter, even if the husband was known to be trustworthy (thiqah). As for ages of physical and mental maturity then they are not fixed and vary from era to era and place to place. Prior to the 19th century the age-based distinctions of “child”, “youth”, “teen”, “adult” never existed, and girls and boys became women and men at puberty which coincided with full mental maturity due to the socio-economic conditions in past societies. In fact, frequently, boys and girls became fully mentally mature before any signs of puberty appeared. The delayed onset of “adulthood”—a modern invention—and mental maturity is a recent phenomena. For more details refer to this article. Since mental and physical maturity are variables which greatly differ between individuals in one society and also between individuals across many societies and eras, Islām does not specify any age for marriage. Rather, this is left to the customs and norms of each society which vary due to economic, social and cultural factors. In the modern era, with delayed onset of maturity, “marriageable age” has risen. Considering this, the laws of Islām in this regard are based upon actual ground realities and upon the fundamental facts of human nature and are universal for all times and places. What has preceded can be explained further by the following scenarios: — 1. Lets say, in 18th century Europe, or the colonies in 19th century America when marriageable age was much lower, going as low as the age of 7 in some places. that the parents of an 8 year old girl get her married to a 14 year old boy—as they find him to be an ideal partner, from a well-to-do family. However, they do not allow cohabitation. Five years later, when she is 13, and her husband is 19, they allow cohabitation. The girl at this age is physically able to engage in sexual intercourse, even though she has not started menstruation. So the couple enjoy conjugal relations. However, six months into the marriage, the 19 year old husband—for whatever reason—decides to divorce her and end the marriage. If Islāmic law was being followed, there would be a three month waiting period for this young lady before the divorce is complete. — 2. The parents of a 14 year old girl in the US allow her to get married to a 19 year old man—this is currently legal in many states in the US—and they allow cohabitation. The girl has not yet menstruated and will not do so until the age of 16. The couple have sexual relations, however the man decides to divorce due to unhappiness in the marriage. Or it could be possible that for some medical reason, she never menstruates at all, and they remain married for 7 years. Then he decides to divorce her. In both of these two situations, if Islāmic law was being followed, there would have to be a three month waiting period to ensure she was not pregnant. If she was, then the divorce would not be complete until after she delivers. — 3. A 26 year old woman marries a 30 year old man. This woman has never menstruated and a couple of years later, the man decides to divorce her. Her waiting period is also three months. These illustrations make the intent of the law very clear. The verse covers all possibilities in relation to marriage and divorce and accommodates all social circumstances, in all places, in all times. If in two decades time, the European and American nations lower the age of marriage and consent to 12 years of age—with our knowledge that there will be many girls who will not start menstruating until three or more years later— then Islāmic law will accommodate these situations. It is timeless, because it is based on the fundamental facts of human nature and accommodates individual biological variation as well as all socio-economic conditions and scenarios across all cultures of humanity.

And [likewise], those who have not menstruated, this comprises those who have not yet menstruated due to young age and those who have never menstruated at all, and this is present among the women, where some of them die after having never menstruated. [Likewise], those who reach the time of menstruating and the [signs] of maturity, but she has not menstruated.
65:4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Andalūsī (d. 754H)

65:4.text: Women who never menstruate at all (a condition called primary amenorrhea) do exist, though not common. Around 2% of girls do not start menstruation even by the age of 15 years and overall less than 1% of women suffer primary amenorrhea, meaning, they have not had a period. The legislation of Islām is all-inclusive and comprehensive and accommodates such people in the application of laws which are legislated for humanity's beneficial interests.

67:10.text: Sins corrupt the intellect, for the intellect has light and sins inevitably extinguish the light of intellect. And when its light is extinguished it weakens and diminishes. Some of the Salaf said: ‘No one [continues to] disobey Allāh until his intellect becomes clouded.’
67:10.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

69:46.text: Christian apologists claim that this verse is a proof that the Prophet was a false prophet because of a statement he made regarding his poisoning by a Jewish woman, whose lingering effects on his health played a role in his death. He said: “I feel as if my vein (abhar) is being cut from that poison.” Al-Bukhārī (no. 4428). The response to this doubt is that this verse was revealed three years before the death of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). The threat in the verse is for lying, and claiming revelation falsely. So if that occurred from him, he would have died through that route straight away, because the condition for the threat was fulfilled. However, Allāh allowed him to continue lying for three more years, if we accept the claim. Al-Ṭabarī said that Allāh would have hastened the punishment, i.e., straight away, and that this is the meaning of the verse. Also, how did Allāh allow the Prophet to claim revelation, and call to it and fight over it for 20 years prior? On the contrary, Allāh supported him with miracles throughout this period! Also that type of poison has an immediate effect, which is why the companion, Ziyad bin Bishr, who also ate of the poisoned lamb with the Prophet died very quickly. However, Allāh strengthened the Prophet’s body allowing him to endure the poisoning. So if Ziyad died straight away, why did the Prophet not also die? Further, if the Prophet was a liar, then what motive does a liar have to insert such a verse into revelation, and why did he not conceal it and not express it at all? Also, in the verse the word “watin” is used, which is the aorta of the heart, the main artery supplying oxygenated blood to the heart. As for “abhar”, then that is a vein and other than the aorta, and there are two of them that carry the blood that is in the veins to the heart. Also, in the verse it says, “if he fabricated some sayings”, putting aside some sayings (i.e. verses), how did Allāh leave him to fabricate a whole Qurʾān over a period of 20 years, and which, in His prior knowledge, would be propagated thereafter, for centuries on end and to billions of people? Also, using this argument implies acceptance that the Qurʾān is the word of Allāh. Hence, the doubt is baseless and self-defeating.

74:31.text: This is the state of the hearts when truth is presented to them: —A heart that is put to trial by it, with disbelief and wilful denial. —A heart that is increased by it in belief and faith. —A heart that becomes certain about it, whereby the proof is established against it. —And a heart that is confused and blinded by it, not knowing what is intended by it.
74:31.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (751H)

78:40.text: It is said: The disbeliever mentioned here is Iblīs (Satan). And that is because he belittled Ādam in that he was created from dust and he boasted of being created from fire. So on the Day of Judgement, when he sees Ādam, and his believing offspring in reward and mercy, and what he is in of severity and punishment, he will say: “How I wish that I were dust.” Abū Hurayrah said: “The dust will say: ‘No, and you have no honour. What made you similar to me?’”
78:40.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

79:40.text: Ibn Masʿūd said: “You are in a time when truth leads the desire, and there will come a time when desire leads the truth. So we seek refuge from that time.”
79:40.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

80:36.text: Al-Ḥasan said: “The first who will flee on the Day of Resurrection from his father is Ibrāhīm. And the first who will free from his son is Nūḥ. And the first who will flee from his wife is Lūṭ.”
80:36.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

81:7.text: From al-Nuʿmān bin Bashīr who said: “A righteous man will be joined with a righteous man in Paradise, and an evil man will be joined with an evil man in Hellfire.” And from al-Ḥasan and Qatādah: “Every man will be put with his group, the Jew with the Jew, the Christian with the Christian.” Al-Rabīʿ bin Khaytham said: “A man will be raised along with a man who did the same actions as him.” And it is said that souls will be paired together on the basis of their actions. And ʿAṭāʾ and Muqātil said: “The souls of the believers will be paired with the Ḥourī [women of Paradise] and the souls of the disbelievers will be paired with the devils.” And ʿIkrimah said: “When the souls will be returned into their bodies.” Editorial note: And the meaning of this last statement of ʿIkrimah is that just as souls were paired with their respective bodies in the world, they will be paired together again with the same bodies on the Day of Resurrection.
81:7.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

86:6.text: Al-Baghawī (d. 516H): Meaning, ejected, poured into the womb. Al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H): al-Dafq means pouring of fluid... al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash said: ‘From water ejected, meaning poured into the womb’. Al-Zajjāj said: ‘From fluid that has been subject to ejection.’

86:7.text: According to some commentators, the pronoun in the verb (يَخْرُجُ) can refer to either the emitted fluid or the human. Al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H): The pronoun in (يخرج) is for the fluid, and it is for the human (in the view of those) who say: ‘between the back of the man and ribs of the woman.’ Ibn ʿAṭiyyah (d. 546H): The pronoun in (يخرج) can refer to the human and it can also refer to the fluid.

According to some commentators, the pronoun in the verb (يخرج) can refer to either a) the ejected fluid (ماء دافق) mentioned in the previous verse, or b) to the human (الإنسان) mentioned in the verse prior to that. Upon this, the verse—through a subtle, multilayered expression—captures the physiology and neurology of ejaculation (which involves the spine), impregnation (lodging of sperm), birth (when the baby comes out from between the spine and lower ribs of the woman) and in an overall sense, the emergence of another human from between the spine of the man and the lower ribs of the woman. All of these processes comprise a sign among the signs of Allāh—human reproduction—which humans are asked to reflect upon in this verse because it points to the plausibility of resurrection. As for the two views mentioned above regarding what the pronoun refers back to and the various explanations resulting from that, then in the first case a), both the backbone and lower ribs refer to those of the man. In the second case b), it can be i) that the backbone is that of the man and the lower ribs are those of the woman or ii) that the backbone and lower ribs are of both the man and the woman. Hence, there are three layers of meaning incorporated, all sitting on top of each other: —1. That the fluid of the male is emitted and expelled from the region between his lower back (spinal cord) and the lower ribs. Meaning, whatever is below the lowest ribs at the front and above the end of the spinal cord at the back. —2. That the child emerges from between the backbone of the man and the lower ribs of the woman. This expression captures all the biology and physiology involved in sexual reproduction and birth. Thus, the male ejects his fluid during copulation (which involves his back) and the child remains under the ribs of the woman until it is delivered. Hence, the child emerged from between the back of the man and the lower ribs of the woman. —3. Similar to the above, that the child emerges as a combined result of what is between a man’s back (lower spine) and front (lower ribs) and what is between a woman’s back (lower spine) and front (lower ribs).

98:4.text: Meaning, of the Jews and Christians. The People of the Book were specified with splitting as opposed to those besides them—even though they both gathered together with the disbelievers [of all types]—because they are presumed to have knowledge. So if they split [alongside knowledge], then those without a book are more worthy of this description. Until after the clear evidence had come to them. Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) is intended by this. Meaning, the Qurʾān is in agreement with what they have in their hands with respect to his [the Prophet’s] qualities and descriptions. This is because they were in agreement about his prophethood [prior to it] but when he was ordered to invite them, they rejected his prophethood, and then split among themselves. So some disbelieved out of envy and jealousy, and others believed, as occurs in the Exalted’saying: And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them, out of jealous animosity between themselves (42:14:). It is also said that “bayyinah” means the discourse in their books that he is a prophet that will be sent, and that His saying And they did not become divided... is His judgement upon the one from the People of the Book who did not believe after the establishment of the proof.
98:4.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

98:6.text: And the intent, it is said, is that they were the worst of creation in [terms of] deeds, and thus, the sentence [at the end of the verse] is in the context of providing the explanatory cause for them remaining in the Hellfire. It is also said [regarding “worst of creatures”] that they are the worst of them in terms of position and destination on that Day, and [the sentence therefore] is an emphasis of their horrid situation. Al-Alūsī goes on to explain the deeds which led to them to this horrid position and they are: Their disbelief despite their sure knowledge of the prophethood of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) from their scriptures, breaking the covenant they had taken that they would follow him when he appears, their misguiding of huge numbers of people through their disbelief and casting doubt into the hearts of others, their distorting scripture, colluding and waging war against him and hindering people from his message.
98:6.author: Maḥmūd al-Alūsī (d. 1270H)

98:6.text: And a people said: Meaning, they are the worst of creatures among those in the era of the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), just as He the Exalted said [about the Children of Israel]: And that I favoured you over all the worlds (nations) (2:47:). Meaning, the nations of your time. And it is not remote that there were from the disbelievers among the nations before the [era of the Prophet] who were worse than them, such as Firʾaun and those who slaughtered the she-camel of the Prophet Ṣāliḥ.
98:6.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

98:6.text: Editorial Note: The Muslim commentators explain that the deeds of those mentioned in this verse are of the worst kind of deeds that one can commit. Those who steal the mention of the Prophet from past scripture by erasing his name and descriptions are worse than those who steal material things. Those who cut off the path to the truth are worse than the highway robbers who cut off the paths of travel. Those who reject truth after knowledge and erudition are worse than those are ignorant and uncivilised. Those who wage war against a Prophet and his followers for no other reason except that they say ‘Our Lord is one’ are worse than those who suffice with mere rejection and disbelief. Hence, this verse is speaking about a group of people in a given era, in particular those who rejected the Prophets and Messengers who came to them in person and did evil, oppressive deeds towards them. Such people’s actions are rightfully referred to as the worst of actions and their situation and outcome on the Final Day will be the worst of situations and outcomes. As for those Islām haters who try to use this verse to make it appear that the Qurʾān is a book of hate and violence, then this is from their ignorance, desires and foolishness—traits that they share with the Khārijite extremists who are known by orthodox Muslims as those who twist, misinterpret and misapply the verses of the Qurʾān. Rather, the Qurʾān is a book of illumination, guidance and justice. This verse is speaking about a specific group of people who committed criminal, oppressive and violent deeds against the Prophet Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and whose situation and outcome will be an evil one in the Hereafter.

109:2.text: The intent here is to mention the deity that is described as being worthy of worship, rightfully deserving of it. Thus, He brought [the particle] mā (ما) which indicates this meaning. As if it is said: And nor are you worshippers of my deity who is described as being the only deity worthy of worship in truth. And if He had brought the particle man (من), then it would have indicated the essence (dhāt) only [of the one being worshipped, and not His attribute].
109:2.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

109:2.text: The particle mā (ما) indicates an attribute (ṣifah) as opposed to [the particle] man (من), for that indicates an entity (ʿayn).
109:2.author: Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728H)

109:2.text: That everyone who does not believe in what the Messenger described Him with, then in reality, he has not worshipped whatever the Messenger worshipped, from that angle. And then analogise with this...
109:2.author: Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728H)

113:2.text: The evil mentioned in this verse is attributed to whatever actions are performed by the creation and not to the Exalted Lord's act of creating [the actions of the servants], which is His action. For there is no evil within [His action] from any angle. Evil does not enter into any of His attributes or actions, just as it is not ascribed to His essence, the Blessed and Exalted... And that which He does of justice towards His servants, and punishing the one who deserves punishment among them, it is pure goodness because it is pure justice and wisdom. It is only evil as it relates to them, when such affairs befall them and take place with respect to them, but not in the act [of creating, rewarding or punishing] that is established with Him. And we do not deny that evil exists within that which He creates, for He is the Creator of both good and evil.
113:2.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)
